GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA 
REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2000 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
GROUNDWATER EXTRACTION IN PUNJAB 
2000.  Smt. HARSIMRAT KAUR BADAL: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that Punjab has  the highest rate of 
groundwater extraction in the country with over 75 per cent of its blocks 
classified as overexploited and groundwater extract ion reaching 156 per cent 
and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the steps taken by the Government to address th e widespread 
contamination of groundwater in Punjab with toxic s ubstances such as 
arsenic, fluoride and uranium as reported in several districts; 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any studie s or assessments on the 
impact of declining groundwater levels and increasi ng salinity on agricultural 
productivity and public health in Punjab and if so,  the details and the key 
findings thereof; and 
(d) the measures being implemented to promote susta inable irrigation 
practices in Punjab given the heavy reliance on tub ewells and reduction in 
canal irrigated area? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 

2 
 
(a)  Dynamic Ground Water Resources of the country are assessed annually 
jointly by Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) and St ate Governments. As per 
the 2025 assessment, the total Annual Ground Water Recharge for the state of 
Punjab is 18.60 Billion Cubic Meter (BCM) and the A nnual Extractable Ground 
Water Resources is estimated as 16.80 BCM. Further,  total Annual Ground 
Water Extraction in Punjab in 2025 has been assesse d as 26.27 BCM. Based on 
this, the Stage of Ground Water Extraction (SoE), which is a measure of Annual 
Ground Water Extraction for all uses (irrigation, i ndustrial and domestic uses) 
over Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource is wo rked out to be 156.36% 
for the state of Punjab. 
Further, 111 (72.55%) blocks out of 153 in Punjab h ave been categorized 
as ‘Over-exploited’ where total annual ground water  extraction exceeds the 
extractable ground water resources. Additionally, 1 0 Blocks are in critical, 15 
in Semi-critical and 17 in Safe category. 
However, groundwater is a  replenishable resource w hich gets recharged 
every year through rainfall and other sources.  Fur ther its sustainability can be 
improved through  judicious regulation of extractio n, artificial recharge and 
large-scale conservation measures. 
(b)  CGWB generates groundwater quality data on a r egional scale across the 
country, including for the state of Punjab, under i ts groundwater quality 
monitoring programme and other scientific studies c onducted by it as per the 
approved Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). As per  the Annual Ground 
Water Quality report 2025, localized occurrence of Arsenic, Fluoride and 
Uranium in ground water in excess of the limits pre scribed for drinking water 
use has been reported in some isolated pockets of Punjab. 
Water is a State subject and the responsibility of taking initiatives to 
mitigate ground water contamination lies primarily with the state 

3 
 
governments. However, to complement the efforts of the state governments, 
several steps have been taken by the Central Govern ment to address these 
issues across the country including Punjab. Some of  the important ones are 
mentioned below:- 
i. The ground water quality data generated by CGWB inc luding that for 
heavy metal contamination, is regularly disseminate d through Annual 
Reports, Half-yearly Bulletins and Fortnightly Aler ts for quick action 
by the stakeholders. 
ii. In order to enhance monitoring efficiency, a new St andard Operating 
Procedure (SoP) for Groundwater Quality Monitoring has been 
adopted by CGWB, which stipulates more frequent and  denser 
sampling, particularly in vulnerable areas, to ensu re a more 
comprehensive assessment of groundwater quality. 
iii. CGWB has also developed an innovative cement sealin g technology 
for tapping deeper Arsenic free aquifers in the Ars enic affected areas 
and has so far successfully constructed 525 Arsenic  safe exploratory 
wells and is also providing technical assistance to  state departments 
for taking up similar constructions. 
iv. Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) – Har Ghar Jal, being impl emented by this 
Ministry in partnership with states, marks an impor tant milestone for 
providing contamination free potable tap water to e very rural 
household of the country in adequate quantity, of p rescribed quality 
and on regular & long-term basis. Several water qua lity safety 
measures including setting up of an extensive netwo rk of testing 
labs, distribution of Field Testing Kits (FTKs), in stallation of 

4 
 
community water purifier plants in affected habitat ions etc. have 
been taken up under JJM. 
v. Improvement in ground water quality can also be ach ieved to some 
extent by taking up artificial recharge of contamin ated aquifers, 
which dilutes the contaminants to reduce their adve rse effects. 
Accordingly, Ministry of Jal Shakti and other centr al ministries are 
implementing several programmes towards this end li ke the annual 
Jal Shakti Abhiyan campaign, Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagid ari (JSJB) 
initiative, PMKSY schemes, etc. 
(c)  CGWB regularly monitors groundwater levels and  groundwater quality 
throughout the country, including Punjab, as per it s mandate. Further, under 
Phase 1.0 of the National Aquifer Mapping and Manag ement Programme 
(NAQUIM), the entire identified mappable area of ab out 25 lakh sq. km of the 
country, including about 50,368 sq. km in Punjab, h as been mapped and 
district-wise groundwater management plans have bee n prepared and shared 
with the concerned State and district authorities f or suitable field-level 
interventions. In the NAQUIM study reports, the pro blem of ground water 
depletion and quality issues like salinity in affec ted pockets has been 
addressed and suitable supply and demand side measu res for remediation like 
construction of rain water harvesting and artificia l recharge structures, 
increasing the area under micro-irrigation, crop di versification etc. have been 
recommended. Similarly, several remedial measures f or mitigation of ground 
water contamination issues like identifying and tap ping safer aquifers for 
drinking water use, various techniques for local wa ter purification etc. have 
also been suggested for preventing adverse impact on public health. 

5 
 
(d) The government has taken up several important m easures, as summarized 
below, for reducing dependence on ground water for irrigation, encouraging 
conjunctive use with surface water and promoting su stainable irrigation 
practices in the country, including Punjab. 
  
i. Under various components of the umbrella Scheme of PMKSY like 
Repair, Renovation & Restoration (RRR), Surface Min or Irrigation 
(SMI) etc. the M/o Jal Shakti provides assistance t o states, including 
Punjab for reviving/restoring traditional water bod ies and enhancing 
irrigation through smaller surface water projects l ike tanks, check 
dams and lift irrigation, benefiting small & marginal farmers. 
ii. As intimated by the Government of Punjab, several m easures have 
been undertaken to promote sustainable irrigation p ractices through 
expansion and modernization of the canal irrigation  system. During 
the last four financial years (2022–26), irrigation  infrastructure 
development works worth more than Rs. 7,200 crore h ave been 
undertaken, including restoration and lining of can als, rehabilitation 
and construction of watercourses, strengthening of underground 
pipeline systems in Kandi areas and modernization o f major canal 
systems. These works have restored canal irrigation  in about 2.75 
lakh acres and enabled canal water to reach several  tail-end and 
previously uncovered areas. 
In addition, the State Government has undertaken me asures such as 
extension of existing canals, restoration of the Ka ndi Canal System, 
implementation of lift irrigation schemes, promotio n of micro-
irrigation and revision of canal water policies to promote greater 

6 
 
utilisation of surface water and efficient irrigati on practices. The 
water allowance in major canal systems has also bee n enhanced to 
improve the availability of canal irrigation. 
iii. Based on the advisories of M/o Jal Shakti to States  to review their 
free/subsidized electricity policy to farmers, brin g suitable water 
pricing policy and to work further towards crop 
rotation/diversification/other initiatives to reduc e over-dependence on 
groundwater, Department of Agriculture, Punjab is p ursuing hard to 
diversify the acreage under paddy to other less wat er consuming 
crops by extending incentives to farmers. 
iv. Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare (DA & FW), GoI, is 
implementing Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) Scheme in th e country 
including Punjab, since 2015-16, which focuses on e nhancing water 
use efficiency at farm level through Micro Irrigati on and better on-
farm water management practices to optimize the use  of available 
water resources.

LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2001 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 30th July, 2026 
 
DOMESTIC PNG EXPANSION UNDER CGD 
 
2001. SHRI KALI CHARAN SINGH: 
 
पेटŌ ोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has intensified efforts to promote the use of Piped Natural Gas (PNG) for 
domestic consumers to reduce dependence on Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) and strengthen India's 
energy security, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the targets fixed for providing domestic PNG connections under the City Gas Distribution (CGD) 
network up to 30 June, 2026 and the number of PNG connections actually released, Geographical 
area-wise and State/UT-wise; 
(c) the names of CGD entities which have failed to achieve the minimum work programme and PNG 
connection targets along with the reasons therefor and the action taken or proposed to be taken against 
such entities thereon; 
(d) whether the Government has prepared a roadmap for expansion of domestic PNG connections 
during the next three years from July 2026 to June 2029, if so, the details of targets thereof, year-wise 
and State/UT-wise; and 
(e) whether the Government has issued or proposes to issue any policy or advisory regarding 
discontinuation, restriction or non-refill of LPG connections in areas where PNG has become 
available, if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुरेश गोपी ) 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (e) Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections is part of the development of City Gas 
Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter alia include creation of pipeline infrastructure and other 
facilities for the supply of PNG to domestic, commercial and industrial units. This is being carried out 
by entities authorized by Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). After completion 
of 12/12A CGD bidding round, PNGRB has authorized entities for the development of CGD network 
in 309 Geographical Areas (GAs), covering the entire mainland area of the country. As on 
31.05.2026, the authorized CGD entities have provided 1,70,69,775 PNG (D) connections across the 
country against the Minimum Work Programme (MWP) targets of 12,65,41,862 PNG (D) connections 
to be achieved by 2034. CGD infrastructure rollout is undertaken by the authorized entities in 
accordance with the authorization granted by PNGRB and the approved project plan. The GA-wise 
and state/UT wise PNG (D) connections progress, as on 31.05.2026, is at Annexure-I and Annexure-
II respectively. 
As informed by authorized CGD entities, challenges in achieving MWP primary include: 
(i) High capital investment requirements for development of CGD infrastructure, particularly 
in sparsely populated and remote areas. 

(ii) Delay in obtaining statutory permissions/Right of Use (RoU)/Right of Way (RoW) and 
other approvals from various Central, State and local authorities for laying pipelines and 
establishing CNG stations. 
(iii) Land availability for installation of CNG stations, City Gate Stations (CGS) and other 
associated infrastructure. 
(iv) Availability and timely connectivity to the Natural Gas pipeline network, especially in 
areas where trunk pipeline infrastructure is under development. 
(v) Geographical and terrain-related constraints, including hilly, forest, coastal and difficult-
to-access areas, which increase project complexity and cost. 
To accelerate the expansion of PNG Domestic connections across the country, PNGRB launched the 
National PNG Drive 2.0 from 1st January 2026 to 30th June 2026, during which 13,37,911 active 
PNG (Domestic) connections were added across the country. 
The progress of CGD networks is monitored regularly through reports submitted by CGD entities. In 
cases of delay or shortfall, entities are advised to take corrective measures. This includes convening 
progress review meetings or statutory hearings, as provided under applicable regulations, to discuss 
challenges and review the latest status of Minimum Work Programme (MWP) targets in their 
authorized GAs and issuance of notices to defaulting entities directing compliance with the terms and 
conditions of authorization and informing them of regulatory action, including penalties, in case of 
continued default. Additionally, the Government holds regular interactions and meetings with State 
Governments to support the development of CGD networks in their respective states and to address 
related challenges. 
The Government has notified a comprehensive control order dated 24.03.2026 under the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 to facilitate time-bound expansion of pipeline infrastructure across the 
country, especially CGD. The Order provides a uniform framework for grant of right of way (RoW) 
and permissions by mandating strict timelines, enabling deemed approvals in case of delays, and 
prohibiting imposition of unauthorized charges by public authorities. It also addresses access issues in 
residential and private areas by ensuring non-discriminatory and time-bound permissions, thereby 
removing key bottlenecks in pipeline laying.  
Government vide notification published in Gazette of India G.S.R 406(E) dated 25.05.2026 has issued 
Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Supply and Distribution) Amendment Order, 2026 stating 
that a person/household having a domestic LPG connection and subsequently having obtained a piped 
natural gas connection shall not take refills of domestic LPG cylinder and shall also within thirty days 
from date of obtaining a PNG connection, either apply for termination of the LPG connection or take 
a transfer voucher for a future LPG connection in non-PNG area.

(a)  whether the Government proposes to provide modern technology to the traditionally operated 
large-scale brass casting industry in Jalesar in Etah and rural artisans in Kasganj and to establish a special

(b)  the details of any particular action plan formulated under the Scheme of Fund for Regeneration

MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2003 
TO BE ANSWERED ON JULY 30, 2026 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF CITIES AS 'GROWTH HUBS' 
 
NO. 2003 SHRI DINESH CHANDRA YADAV: 
  SHRI KAUSHALENDRA KUMAR: 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the current status of the project to develop cities as "growth hubs" in 
line with the announcement made in the Union Budget 2024-25; and 
(b) whether any city from Bihar has also been selected under the said 
project and if so, the details thereof, city-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) & (b): The Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) scheme has been operationalized 
with the launch of Operational Guidelines for UCF on 15th April, 2026. The 
scheme guidelines are in public domain and may be accessed at  
https://www.mohua.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/04/7950afb9b2d5cb773ba3d
6c64bde9726.pdf  
UCF supports the development and strengthening of urban infrastructure 
through implementation of transformative and impactful projects under 
three verticals namely ‘Cities as Growth Hubs’, ‘Creative Redevelopment of 
Cities’ and ‘Water and Sanitation’. 
So far, 33 projects have been approved/ accorded in-principle approval. No 
proposal has been received from Bihar State for consideration under UCF.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2004 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
 
ELECTRIFIED VILLAGES IN RAJASTHAN 
 
†2004. SHRI BRIJENDRA SINGH OLA: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total number of villages declared electrified by the Government in the 
country so far along with the district -wise details for the State of Rajasthan 
particularly regarding the status of backward areas;  
 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any surve y or inquiry in such 
declared electrified villages to ascertain families/households still without an 
electricity connection despite the presence of electricity poles, transformers 
or sub-stations, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
 
(c) the concrete steps being taken by the Government to ensure that the 
electricity reaches every household in those villages where some families are 
still without power; and  
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to initiate any inquiry and verificatio n 
mechanism in this regard so that electrification on paper translates into 
electricity actually reaching households and if so, the details thereof including 
timeline for the same? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (d): Electricity being a concurrent subject, supply and distribution of 
electricity to all consumers is within the purview of the respective State 
Government/ distribution utility. Government of India (GoI) has been 
supplementing the effort s of the States through various schemes to help 
achieve the objective of providing quality and reliable supply of power to all 
consumers. 
 
 As reported by the States/ UTs, all the inhabited un -electrified census 
villages in the country have been electrified.  A total of 18,374 villages were 
electrified under Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) launched 
in 2014, including 427 villages in the State of Rajasthan ( District wise details 
enclosed at Annexure-I). Under DDUGJY and thereafter during Pradhan  Mantri 
Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) launched in October, 2017, all willing 
households as reported by the States/ UTs were electrified. A total of 2.86 crore 
households were electrified during SAUBHAGYA period including 21,27,728 
households in t he State of Rajasthan. Both the schemes stand closed as on 
31.03.2022. 
 

 Under ongoing Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) launched in 
2021, grid electrification works amounting to Rs. 6,521 crore have been 
sanctioned for 13.65 lakh households, base d on proposal submitted by the 
States post survey, including works for electrification of households belonging 
to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) identified under Pradhan Mantri 
Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), tribal households under DA-
JGUA (Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan), households belonging to 
Scheduled Caste (SC) under Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana 
(PM-AJAY) and households in remote & border areas under Vibrant Villages 
Program (VVP), wherever found feasible (state-wise details are at Annexure–II). 
This includes Rs 1,765 crore sanctioned for electrification of 4.39 lakh 
households in the state of Rajasthan. Out of the sanction at country level, a 
total of 4.87 lakh households have been electrifie d till date including 
approximately 1.31 lakh households in the State of Rajasthan (District wise 
details are enclosed at Annexure-III). 
 
Government of India is taking all necessary steps to support States for 
electrification of all households. Since most of the left -out households are in 
remote, hilly and forest areas, the norms for electrification under RDSS were 
relaxed and the ceiling limit for cost of electrification was enhanced. Grid based 
electrification works have been sanctioned under RDSS whereve r found

the New Solar Power Scheme (for PVTG and Tribal Habitations/Villages) under 
PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA w hich includes electrification of un -electrified 
households (HHs) in PVTG and Tribal habitations/villages in identified tribal 
habitations/villages through off -grid solar systems; where electricity supply 
through grid is not techno-economically feasible.  
 
Under this scheme, as on 30.06.2026, 11,838 households have been 
electrified through solar off -grid systems in ten states. State -wise details are

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2005 
 ANSWERED ON 30/07/2026 
IMPLEMENTATION OF JJM AND JJM 2.0 IN VALSAD 
 
2005. SHRI DHAVAL LAXMANBHAI PATEL: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and JJM 2.0 in Valsad 
Lok Sabha Constituency including coverage of households with functional tap water 
connections; 
(b) the details of water supply schemes, bulk pipelines and infrastructure works completed or 
underway thereof; 
(c) the progress under Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari Abhiyan and Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the 
Rain in Gujarat including the number of water conservation structures created such as borewell 
recharge with community and CSR participation; and 
(d) whether any assessment has been made regarding groundwater recharge and water body 
rejuvenation in Gujarat and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRIV. SOMANNA) 
 
(a) & (b) Drinking Water is a ‘State’ subject, and hence, under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), the 
responsibility of planning, approval, implementation, operation & maintenance of drinking 
water supply schemes lies with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supports the 
States by providing technical and financial assistance. 
Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States/UTs including Gujarat, is 
implementing JJM – Har Ghar Jal to make provision of tap water supply to every rural 
household of the country. The Union Cabinet has approved extension of the JJM up to 
December 2028, with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation framework 
focusing on structural reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. 
As reported by State of Gujarat, as on date, all rural households have been provided with tap 
water connection including those in Valsad Lok Sabha constituency. As numerous projects are 

Page 2 of 6 
 
implemented concurrently at various levels across the States/UTs for achieving the envisaged 
objectives of JJM, project -wise details of individual projects/ schemes for rural water supply 
projects are maintained at the State Government level. 
(c) As informed by the Department of Water Resources, River Development & Gang a 
Rejuvenation, water is a State subject and States are primarily responsible for planning, funding 
and implementing water conservation measures, while the Central Government supplements 
these efforts. 
The Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative was launched on 6 September 2024 to promote 
community-led, low-cost rainwater harvesting through recharge structures such as borewells, 
recharge shafts and pits, supported by community contributions, CSR and convergence with 
Central, State and local schemes. JSJB 2.0 was implemented from 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2026, 
and JSJB: Catch the Rain (CTR)–2026 was launched on 1 June 2026 by integrating JSJB with 
the Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA: CTR) campaign. District-wise progress in Gujarat 
under JSJB 1.0 and 2.0 is at Annexure-I. 
The Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA), launched in 2019 and expanded nationwide as JSA: Catch the 
Rain in 2021 with the message "Catch the Rain: Where It Falls, When It Falls," has evolved 
into a national water conservation campaign with annu al thematic focus. Since 2023, the 
campaign has targeted priority districts for source sustainability, groundwater management and 
community participation. JSA: CTR 2025, themed "Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Jan Jagrukta 
Ki Or," focused on grassroots particip ation, convergence and innovative financing in 148 
CGWB-identified districts. District -wise progress in Gujarat under JSA: CTR 2025 is at 
Annexure-II. 
(d) As informed by DoWR, GR & RD, Dynamic Ground Water Resources of the country 
including Gujarat are assessed every year jointly by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) 
and the State Government. The annual ground water resource assessment provides updated 
estimates of annual groundwater recharge, annual extractable groundwater resources, annual 
groundwater extraction and stage of groundwater extraction and categorizes assessment units 
as Safe, Semi -Critical, Critical and Over -Exploited based on the stage of groundwater 
extraction. A comparison of the Ground Water Resource Assessments for 2017 and 2025 in 
Gujarat indicates that during this period, the Total Annual Ground Water Recharge increased 
from 22.37 BCM to 27.58 BCM, while the Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource 
increased from 21.25 BCM to 25.61 BCM. Although the Annual Ground Water Extraction 
increased from 13.58 BCM to 14.33 BCM, the Stage of Ground Water Extraction declined 
from 63.89% to 55.95%, mainly due to the increase in groundwater recharge and extractable 
resources.

Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

WATER SUSTAINABILITY AND FEEDSTOCK USE IN ETHANOL PRODUCTION 
 
2007. SHRI THIRU D M KATHIR ANAND: 
 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of studies conducted by the Government regarding the water footprint 
associated with ethanol production from sugarcane, maize, paddy and other feedstocks, the 
implications thereof for groundwater resources, irrigation demand, agricultural sustainability 
and water security, with specific reference to Tamil Nadu;  
(b)  the comparative assessment available regarding water consumption, ethanol yield and 
environmental sustainability of various feedstocks used under the Ethanol Blended Petrol 
Programme;  
(c)  the measures adopted/proposed by the Government for encouraging water-efficient 
feedstocks, utilisation of agricultural residues, second-generation biofuels and other 
sustainable alternatives for ethanol production; 
(d)  the details of funds allocated, released and utilised by the Government under ethanol- 
blending, biofuel development and related infrastructure programmes during the last five 
years, year-wise; and 
(e)  the safeguards adopted by the Government to balance energy security objectives with 
concerns relating to food security, water conservation and sustainable agricultural practices? 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏय मंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (e):  An expert committee was constituted in 2024 by Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers 
Welfare to examine the water consumption of various ethanol feedstock crops. The Report has found 
that water requirement is maximum for Rice followed by Maize and Sugarcane.  
The Government has adopted a balanced approach to the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme, 
ensuring that water sustainability, food security and farmers' interests remain paramount. 
The Government follows a diversified feedstock strategy under the National Policy on Biofuels. 
Ethanol is produced from multiple approved feedstocks, including sugarcane-based feedstocks, 
maize, damaged foodgrains, broken rice, foodgrains unfit for human consumption, surplus 
foodgrains approved by the National Biofuel Coordination Committee (NBCC) and other approved 
agricultural feedstocks. The Government is also promoting Second Generation (2G) ethanol from 
agricultural residues under the Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana to progressively increase the use of 
non-food feedstocks. 
The diversion of foodgrains for ethanol production is carefully calibrated in consultation with the 
Department of Food & Public Distribution and other concerned Ministries. Food security, Public 

Distribution System (PDS) requirements, National Food Security Act (NFSA) obligations, Other 
Welfare Schemes (OWS) and prescribed buffer stocks are accorded the highest priority. Only 
surplus foodgrains, after meeting these requirements, are permitted for ethanol production. The 
Government is also promoting crop diversification towards comparatively less water-intensive 
feedstocks such as maize and encouraging sustainable agricultural practices so that expansion of 
ethanol feedstocks remains balanced with the production of pulses, oilseeds and other essential food 
crops. 
Water-use efficiency is also being enhanced through micro-irrigation, drip irrigation and other water 
conservation measures under the Per Drop More Crop component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi 
Sinchayee Yojana. Many sugar mills are also encouraging farmers to adopt water-efficient 
cultivation practices. 
Molasses-based distilleries with incineration boilers and grain-based distilleries are required to 
operate as Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) units, enabling recycling and reuse of process water while 
eliminating liquid effluent discharge. Modern ethanol plants typically consume about 3–5 litres of 
processed water for producing one litre of ethanol. 
The details of funds allocated, released and utilised for bio-ethanol (2G) project under PM JI-VIAN 
Yojana are as under :

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2008 
TO BE ANSWERED ON JULY 30, 2026 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF SCM AND AMRUT 
 
NO. 2008 SHRI VIJAYAKUMAR ALIAS VIJAY VASANTH: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether municipal bodies are adequately equipped to manage 
increasing population pressures and if so, the details thereof 
including the financial and technical resources available along 
with the steps taken to strengthen Urban Local Governance 
capacity; 
(b) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of 
Smart Cities Mission (SCM) and Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and 
Urban Transformation (AMRUT) in addressing infrastructure gaps 
and if so, the details thereof along with the outcomes achieved 
in improving urban living conditions; 
(c) whether informal settlements and slums have expanded due to 
migration and if so, the details thereof along with the measures 
taken to provide affordable housing and basic services to urban 
poor populations; 
(d) whether the Government has taken steps to integrate urban 
planning with population growth projections and if so, the details 
thereof along with the strategies adopted to ensure sustainable 
and inclusive city development; and 
(e) whether climate change impacts are aggravating urban 
infrastructure challenges and if so, the details thereof along with 
the measures taken to build resilient infrastructure and disaster 
preparedness in cities?   
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a):  As per entry 5 of List II -  State List of the Seventh Schedule of 
the Constitution of India, Local Government, that is to say, the 
constitution and powers of municipal corporations, improvement  
…2/- 
 

-2- 
trusts, districts boards, mining settlement authorities and other local 
authorities for the purposes of local self -government or village 
administration, is a state subject. The Government of India 
supplements the efforts of States/ Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) through 
programmatical assistance, policy support, technical guidance and 
capacity-building initiatives to enhance the effectiveness of Urban 
Local Bodies. 
The Government has undertaken several initiatives to strengthen the 
financial, technical and institutional capacity of ULBs to address the 
challenges arising from rapid urbanisation and the increasing demand 
for urban services.   Under the Fifteenth Finance Commission (XV FC) 
award period (2021–26), grants of around ₹94,000 crore had been 
released to ULBs across 28 States. The XV FC framework incentivised 
States and ULBs to undertake key municipal finance and governance 
reforms through performance- linked grant releases. Consequently, 23 
States had notified or revised f loor rates of property tax, while 3,866 
ULBs met the eligibility requirement of achieving annual growth in 
property tax collection at least equal to the average growth rate of the 
respective State’s Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) over the 
preceding f ive years for claiming grants in FY 2025- 26. The 
Commission also promoted timely publication of audited accounts, 
standardised municipal financial reporting, disclosure of SLBs and 
digital monitoring of grants through the City Finance Portal, thereby 
enhancing transparency, accountability and financial management. 
 
(b): Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 
launched in the year 2015 in selected 500 cities and towns across the 
country was focused on development of basic infrastructure, in the 
selected cities and towns, in the sectors of water suppl y, sewerage 
and septage management, storm water drainage, parks and green 
spaces, etc. To expand the coverage, AMRUT 2.0 is launched in the 
year 2021 in all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ cities, enabling the cities 
to become 'self -reliant' and 'water secure'.  Providing universal 
coverage of sewerage and septage management in 500 AMRUT cities 
is one of the major focus areas of AMRUT 2.0. Water body rejuvenation 
and green spaces and parks are other components of AMRUT 2.0. 
Under the Mission, States/ Union Territories (UTs) are empowered to 
select, appraise, prioritize and implement projects. 
…3/- 

-3- 
Under AMRUT, States/UTs have grounded 6,007 projects worth 
₹83,491.77 crore which includes, 1,411 water supply projects worth 
₹43,372.06 crore, 888 Sewerage & Septage Management projects 
worth ₹34,471.71 crore, 838 storm water drainage projects worth 
₹3,022.39 crore and 2,522 parks projects worth ₹1,604.13 crore. 
Under AMRUT 2.0 so far, State Water Action Plans of all the States/UTs 
comprising of  8,777 projects worth ₹1,97,191.86 crore have been 
approved, which includes 3,572 water supply projects worth 
₹1,18,968.38 crore, 605 Sewerage & Septage Management projects 
worth ₹71,133.01 crore, 2,951 water body rejuvenation projects worth 
₹6,003.34 crore and 1,649 parks projects worth ₹1,087.12 crore. 
Through AMRUT/ AMRUT 2.0 and in convergence with the States, 
around 270 lakh water tap connections in the urban areas have been 
provided, 1.12 lakh km of water pipeline network has been laid/ 
replaced and 5,611 Million Litre per Day (MLD) water treatment 
capacity have been developed. In the sewage and septage 
management sector, around 197 lakh sewer connections (including 
households covered through Faecal Sludge and Septage Management 
(FSSM)) have been provided in AMRUT Cities, 28,589 km of sewer 
network has been laid/ replaced completed and 6,017 MLD sewage 
treatment capacity has been developed. 
NITI Aayog in its report titled ‘Evaluation of Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes in Package 4 – Urban Transformation and Skill Development’ 
of September 2025, has stated that the AMRUT missions have led to 
visible, and sustained improvements in service delivery,  institutional 
capacity, and citizen wellbeing across Indian cities. The mission’s 
long-term effects are most evident in improved governance culture, 
women’s empowerment, and resilience against urban service gaps. 
The objective of Smart City Mission (SCM) was to follow an area-based 
development approach through retrofitting, redevelopment, greenfield 
development and a Pan- city initiative in which smart solutions are 
applied covering larger parts of the city, so as t o create a replicable 
model. The cities under SCM were developed based on Smart City 
Proposals (SCPs) received from States/UTs, across various sectors, 
viz., smart mobility, Water Sanitation Hygiene (WASH), smart  
…4/- 
 
 

-4- 
governance, smart energy, environment etc., approved by High 
Powered Steering Committee (HPSC) chaired by the Chief Secretary. 
NITI Aayog in the evaluation report has concluded that the Smart Cities 
Mission demonstrates strong alignment with national urban priorities 
and citizen needs, contributing significantly to multiple United Nations 
Sustainable Development Goals. As per the report, the Mission has 
achieved a high project completion rate of 93% of 8,063 projects and 
100% completion of Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs), 
leading to measurable improvements in urban liveability, mobility, 
safety, and environmental outcomes. 
 
(c):   Land' and 'Colonization' are State subjects. Therefore, schemes 
related to housing for their citizens are implemented by States/Union 
Territories (UTs). However, MoHUA  supplements the efforts of 
States/UTs, by providing Central Assistance for pucca houses to 
eligible urban beneficiaries across the country under Pradhan Mantri 
Awas Yojana-  Urban (PMAY -U) since 25.06.2015. Based on the 
learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY -U, MoHUA 
has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 'Housing for All' 
Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban areas 
across the country to construct, purchase and rent a house by eligible 
beneficiaries at aff ordable cost, for 1 crore additional eligible 
beneficiaries through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led Construction 
(BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental 
Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS).  
PMAY-U  &  P M A Y-U 2.0 are demand driven scheme. Selection of 
beneficiaries, under various verticals preferred by the beneficiaries, 
formulation of projects and execution including allotment of 
completed houses to the eligible beneficiaries are done by States/UTs. 
The Ministry conducts regular reviews with the States/UTs to monitor 
progress of implementation of the scheme and expedite completion of 
sanctioned houses within the stipulated timeline. 
In order to enhance the affordability of the houses, State/UT share is 
mandatory under PMAY-U 2.0. Apart from the minimum State/UT share,  
…5/- 
 
 
 

-5- 
the State/UT Governments may also provide additional top-up share to 
increase affordability. 
PMAY-U 2.0 supports States/UTs for formulation and implementation of 
‘Affordable Housing Policies’ to incentivize private sector participation 
through appropriate regulatory, fiscal and institutional measures to 
make the housing stock affordable in urban areas.  
 
(d) and (e) :   Water, sanitation, Land and Colonization are State 
subjects. Further, as per the 12th Schedule of the Constitution, Urban 
Planning including Town Planning is the responsibility of Urban Local 
Bodies (ULBs)/ Urban Development Authorities. Government of India 
supplements the efforts of the States through schematic interventions/ 
advisories. It provides financial and technical support to the States for 
sustainable and inclusive growth of the cities/ towns through various 
schemes/ Missions such as Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban 
Transformation (AMRUT)/ AMRUT 2.0, Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) 
2.0 (SBM-U 2.0), Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) (PMAY-U)/ PMAY-
U 2.0, Metro Rail/ Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS), Urban 
Challenge Fund, etc. 
The water supply, sewerage and septage management and other 
infrastructure projects under various Missions/ scheme of MoHUA are 
designed by the States/ UTs based on the projected future growth of 
the cities/ towns.  
The Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India 
has issued Urban and Regional Development Plan Formulation and 
Implementation (URDPFI) Guidelines, 2014 
(https://www.mohua.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/10/1813403503fbec280
e7648c0ae692512.pdf).  The Chapter -  6 “Sustainable Guidelines” of 
URDPFI guidelines 2014 deals with sustainable development.

2009.    SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY              
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the extent to which flight operations in the country have been curtailed due to the fuel 
shortage resulting from the conflict in Gulf nations; 
 
(b) whether there are signs of the fuel crisis being resolved and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether the suspended flight operations would be resumed as usual and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
 
(d) the details of the Government's plan to launch the Mangaluru -Tirupati flight service, a 
long-standing demand of devotees? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a): As informed by the Indian scheduled carriers, they have not curtailed flight operations 
due to shortage of aviation fuel.; 
 
(b) & (c): Does not arise.;

route/city based on market demand, commercial feasibility and their company policy.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2010 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
  
APPROVED COLD CHAIN PROJECTS  
  
2010.  SHRI ANTO ANTONY:  
  
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the details of the total number of Cold Chain projects approved in each State, along 
with the number of projects completed and currently under implementation, State-wise; 
(b)  the total amount of funds approved, released and utilized for Cold chain projects in each 
State, State-wise; 
(c)  the number of Cold Chain projects approved in each State that were sanctioned more 
than five years ago and more than ten years ago, State-wise; 
(d)  the reasons for delay, if any in completion of Cold Chain projects approved more than 
five years ago and more than ten years ago; 
(e)  the total amount of funds approved for ongoing Cold Chain projects in Kerala along 
with the amount released and utilized so far; and 
(f)  whether there have been any delay in the release of funds for Cold Chain projects in 
Kerala and if so, the details thereof and the measures taken by the Government to 
address such delays? 
 
  ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing 
Integrated Cold Chain & Value Addition Infrastructure scheme (Cold Chain scheme) since 
2008. As of 30.06.2026, under Cold Chain scheme, 409 Cold Chain projects have been 
approved nationwide with total grants-in-aid of ₹3089.08 crore, of which ₹2540.89 crore has 
already been released for implementation of the projects. Of the 409 projects, 311 have been 
completed and operationalised and 98 are ongoing. A comprehensive State-wise breakup of the 
approved, completed and operational projects, along with the funds approved and released is 
furnished in Annexure-I. 
 (c) & (d): 320 Cold Chain projects were sanctioned more than five years ago [2008-09 to 
2020-21] including 25 ongoing projects. 125 Cold Chain projects were sanctioned more than 
ten years ago [2008-09 to 2015-16] including three ongoing projects. State-wise breakup of the 
same is furnished at Annexure-II.  

 
The following reasons are attributed for delay in completion of the above mentioned 25 
ongoing projects sanctioned more than five years ago and three ongoing projects sanctioned 
ten years ago:  
            (i) Delay in obtaining statutory approvals from local bodies and regulatory authorities. 
            (ii) Delay in disbursement of term loan by banks. 
          (iii) Delay in submission of requests by the promoters for change in location of the 
project, change in bank and change in components. 
            (iv) Difficulty in mobilising fund for meeting out promoter’s equity. 
            (v) Delay in receiving imported plant and machinery and installation in the project.  
            (vi) Covid-19 pandemic, which disrupted labour availability, logistics and equipment 
supply.  
            (vii) Delayed submission of claims by the promoter.  
  
(e) & (f): Total grants-in-aid of ₹35.77 crore was approved for four ongoing projects in the 
State of Kerala, of which ₹3.12 crore was released to one project. The major reasons for the 
delay in release of funds to these ongoing projects are: 
            (i) delay in obtaining statutory approvals from local bodies and regulatory authorities. 
 (ii) delay in disbursement of term loan by banks and  
(iii) delay in submission of claims to the Ministry by the promoter. 
  
To address such issues pertaining to delay in implementation of the project, the Ministry 
conducts regular review meetings with the project implementing agencies and helps them in 
mitigating the problems at various levels.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 2011 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
DISRUPTION IN FLIGHT OPERATIONS ON INTERNATIONAL 
ROUTES 
2011.    SMT  JUNE MALIAH                        
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of the evolving security situation and 
armed conflicts in the West Asia/Gulf region on international operations of Indian airlines 
and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of flights rerouted, diverted or cancelled by Indian carriers due to airspace 
restrictions during the last two years, year-wise; 
 
(c) whether the resultant airspace restrictions, route diversions and security advisories have 
affected flight schedules, operational costs, passenger traffic and airfares on services operated 
by Indian carriers to Europe, North America and the Gulf region and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the economic impac t of such 
disruptions on the Indian civil aviation sector including airlines and air cargo operations and 
if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) the measures taken by the Government in coordination with the relevant national and 
international agencies to ensure the safety of passengers and crew, maintain uninterrupted air 
connectivity and mitigate the operational and financial impact on Indian airlines? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a) and (b): The Gov ernment continuously monitored the situation in the West Asia/Gulf 
region. Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued advisories to address and 
ensure the safety of passengers, crew, and aircraft evolving from the risks arising from the 
West A sia conflict. These advisories provide operational guidance on affected airspace, 
including Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), identification of high -risk areas, Flight Information 
Region (FIR) boundaries and impacted countries, enabling operators to plan safe routing after 
conducting comprehensive Safety Risk Assessments. 
 
(c) to (e) : Indian carriers have informed that re -routing of flights has led to increased flight 
durations and higher fuel consumption, resulting in additional operational costs for airlines. 
The extent of such costs depends on route diversion, duration and prevailing fuel prices. 

Further, as informed, airlines are incurring significant revenue losses due to the ongoing 
crisis. Airlines are, however, taking necessary measures to mitigate the impact while ensuring 
continuity of operations. 
; 
A 24*7 Passenger Assistance Control Room was established for real -time coordination and 
passenger support. Passenger assistance was also provided through airport help desks and 
real-time travel updates by airli nes. The Ministry also worked closely with the Ministry of 
External Affairs to address emerging requirements relating to Indian carriers and Indian 
nationals in the region. The Indian Mission in Riyadh, in coordination with Indian Missions 
in Bahrain, Iraq , Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and the UAE, facilitated the transit of affected 
individuals through Saudi Arabia.

FARMERS INCOME 
2012. DR. PRABHA MALLIKARJUN: 
    
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of post -harvest losses 
occurring across agricultural and horticultural commodities in the country and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b) the details of cold chain facilities, food processing units, integrated pack houses, food 
parks and agro-processing infrastructure established during the last five, State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has evaluated the impact of food processing infrastructure on 
farmers income, value addition, employment generation and reduction of wastage and 
if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the measures being taken to strengthen food processing ecosystem s, reduce post -
harvest losses and improve market access for farmers; and 
(e) whether any integrated  food processing, cold -chain, Mega Food Park or agro - 
processing projects have been sanctioned in Karnataka, particularly in Davanagere 
district and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
(a): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) estimates post-harvest losses from 
time to time for various agri-produces in the country through commissioning of studies based 
on primary surveys. Two studies were commissioned by the Ministr y through (i) Indian 
Council of Agriculture Research (ICAR) -Central Institute of Post -Harvest Engineering & 
Technology (CIPHET), 2015 with reference year 2012 -14 and (ii) NABARD Consultancy 
Service Pvt. Ltd (NABCONS), 2022 with reference year 2020-22.  As per the reports of these

(b): Under the Central Sector umbrella scheme - Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana 
(PMKSY), MoFPI provides financial support in the form of grants -in-aid/ subsidy for setting 
up of food processing projects for creating both processing and preservation infrastr ucture 
facilities. Under the components schemes of PMKSY, the details of cold chain facilities, food 
processing units, food parks and agro-processing infrastructure established during the last five, 
state-wise is placed at Annexure-I.   
(c): MoFPI, from time to time, has assessed and has estimated  the processing level s for 
selected commodities to determine the post-harvest losses, to evaluate the implementation and 
impact of its ongoing schemes in order to examine the overall status of food-processing sector 
in the country . However, so far, MoFPI has not undertaken any assessment specifically to 
identify the impact of food processing infrastructure on farmer income, value addition, 
employment generation and reduction of wastage. 
(d): MoFPI through implementation of various initiatives and schemes viz. Pradhan Mantri 
Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY), Prime Minister Formalization of Micro Food Processing 
Enterprises (PMFME) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industries 
(PLISFPI) aims for the overall development of food processing sector across the country. 
MoFPI, through its schemes, provides grant-in-aid/incentives to the eligible entities including 
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) and Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) all 
over the country. These schemes aim towards creation of modern infrastructure with efficient 
supply chain management from farm gate to retail outlet . The schemes include  storage, 
transportation, c reation of market linkages etc.  to help in redu cing post -harvest losses and 
facilitating enhance farmer incomes and creating off-farm employment opportunities. 
Apart from MoFPI, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has launched the 
Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) Scheme in July 2020 under the Atmanirbhar Bharat 
package in order to improve post-harvest infrastructure and create community-farming assets. 
The AIF Scheme facilitates sanction of medium to long term loans by Banks and other lending 
institutions for the setting up of cold storage facilities, warehouses and processing units, aimed 
at reducing crop wastage, enhancing value addition and provide better returns to farmers. 
(e): The details of the projects sanctioned in Karnataka under the component schemes of 
PMKSY are placed in Annexure-II. One project of M/s GEM Food Park LLP under 
Infrastructure for Agro-Processing Clusters Scheme (APC) is located in Davangere district of 
Karnataka with project cost Rs. 40.01 crore.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2013 
TO BE ANSWERED ON JULY 30, 2026 
 
UNAUTHORIZED CONSTRUCTIONS ON PUBLIC LAND 
NO. 2013  SHRI KISHORI LAL:  
PROF. SOUGATA RAY: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the increasing instances of 
unauthorised construction of residential, commercial and institutional 
buildings on public land and encroached Government land in various 
parts of the country, especially in metropolitan cities; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof during the last five years, State/UT-wise; 
(c)  whether the Government has conducted any survey or assessment to 
identify buildings constructed on encroached public land or without 
obtaining mandatory approvals from the competent authorities and if 
so, the details thereof;  
(d)  the action taken against persons, builders, developers and officials 
found responsible for permitting or facilitating such illegal 
constructions; and 
(e)  the measures taken/proposed to be taken to ensure removal of 
unauthorised structures, restoration of public land and 
implementation of transparent, technology-based building permission 
and monitoring systems across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU)   
 
(a) to (e): As per entry 18 and 35 of List II -  State List of the Seventh 
Schedule of the Constitution of India, ‘Land’; ‘Colonization’ and ‘Works, land  
…2/- 

-2- 
and buildings vested in or in the possession of the State’ are State subjects, 
respectively. Further, as per entry 2 of Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution 
of India, ‘Regulation of land-use and construction of buildings’ is the subject 
of Urban Local Bodies  (ULBs). T herefore, t he matters related to illegal 
encroachment of land fall under the jurisdiction of the respective State 
Government/Union Territory  (UT)/ULBs. The State -level authorities use 
applicable laws to remove encroachments on land under their jurisdiction.  
 
However, as far as properties of Land & Development Office (L&DO) of the 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs in Delhi are concerned, cases of 
encroachment are dealt through administrative action and instrumentalities 
like the Public Premises (Eviction of  Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971. 
With respect to Central govt. vacant land parcels of L&DO in other states, 
the same have been assigned to Central Public Works Department (CPWD) 
for care & maintenance. CPWD has informed that cases of encroachments 
have been observed at 20 locations, some of which are under litigations. 
The CPWD regularly monitors the land under its jurisdiction and takes 
measures for removal of encroachments/unauthorised structures through 
legal actions.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 2015 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
MENTAL HEALTH ASSESSMENT OF PILOTS  
2015.    SHRI VISHALDADA PRAKASHBAPU PATIL        
             SHRI SHRIRANG APPA CHANDU BARNE          
             SMT BHARTI PARDHI                       
             SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR            
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has review ed the Fit -to-Fly medical criteria to include 
comprehensive mental health assessments for holders of Commercial Pilot Licences (CPLs); 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the mandatory Peer Support Programmes that airlines 
are required to establish to address pilot burnout; 
 
(c) the mechanism in place for non -punitive reporting of stress -related issues by crew 
members without fear of immediate suspension of licence; 
 
(d) the details of the study conducted by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation ( DGCA) 
on the impact of Ultra -Long Haul flights on the circadian rhythm and mental alertness of 
cockpit crew; 
 
(e) the steps taken to prevent commercial pressure from airlines that may compel pilots to 
operate flights despite reporting fatigue; and 
 
(f) the total number of pilots who have successfully availed departmental counselling services 
since the implementation of the new Flight Duty Time Limitations (FDTL) norms? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a) to (c): Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) vide Medical Circular 01/2023 has 
issued guidelines for Mental Health Promotion of Flight Crew and Air Traffic Control 
Officers (ATCOs). Comprehensive Mental Health Assessment is already a fitness cr iteria to 
obtain medical fitness and all DGCA licences. Assessment of mental health of aircrews is 
conducted as a part of DGCA Medical Examinations on a regular basis. .; 
; 
DGCA undertakes quarterly review of all activities undertaken by major operators to wards 
promotion of mental health.; 

; 
Multiple measures are recommended to ensure availability of timely professional assistance. 
Operators are advised to help aircrews in capacity building through mental health awareness 
seminars, regular training sessions.; 
; 
Peer support program is a non-punitive and proactive program embedded in Medical Circular 
01 of 2023 for promotion of mental health and to assist aircrew in recognizing, coping up and 
overcoming various problems. This program is enshrined with the mec hanism for redressal 
without the fear of loosing any licence privileges upon disclosure of problems. Operators are 
implementing this program in letter and spirit to address pilot burnout and to ensure flight 
safety.; 
; 
(d): No study on such impact was conducted.; 
; 
(e) & (f): Fatigue reports are an important tool for identifying and mitigating crew fatigue. 
DGCA CAR 7/J/III mandates each operator to establish a clear policy on fatigue reporting 
that explains both how to raise a report and how it will be han dled, with executive 
responsibility for fatigue management defined by the operator. 
 
As per the said CAR, all fatigue reports and action-taken reports are to be retained for at least 
one year and made available to DGCA when required. In addition, quarterly  fatigue reports, 
along with analysis and actions taken, is to be submitted to DGCA by the Head of 
Operations. In this year, a total of 22 aircrew have availed departmental counselling services.

NEW WATER PROJECT IN BANKURA DISTRICT 
2016.  Shri SAUMITRA KHAN: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to undertake a new water project in 
Bankura district and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the present status of the said project along wi th the key specifications of 
the proposed micro-dams including their design, cap acity and projected 
benefits; 
(c) the number of villages likely to be benefitted from the said project; and 
(d) whether any sedimentation has been reported in the river after completion 
of the existing irrigation project and if so, the d etails thereof along with the 
agency responsible for dredging and maintenance of the river? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) to (c)   Water, being State subject, water resources project s are planned, 
funded, executed and maintained by the State Govern ments themselves as 
per their own resources and priorities. Role of Gov ernment of India is limited

projects under the ongoing schemes.

stretches for a length of 61.25 km of these three rivers has been taken up with

also generate revenue.

  GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2017 
ANSWERED ON 30th JULY, 2026 
FASTAG ANNUAL PLAN 
†2017. SHRI LALJI VERMA: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of FASTag users currently registered in the country; 
(b) the number of such users covered under the FASTag annual plan of 
Rs. 3,075; 
(c) the number of toll plazas being closed due to the provision of the 
distance of less than sixty kms. on the same route, State-wise; and 
(d) whether the Government has fixed any specific timeline for complete 
replacement of  physical toll plazas across the country with satellite -
based GNSS and automatic number plate  recognition technology to 
enable distance-based toll collection? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) As on June, 2026, about 6.23 crore FASTags  are active across the 
country and are used for electronic toll transactions at National Highway 
fee plazas.  
(b) Annual Pass scheme for non -commercial cars, jeeps, and vans has 
come into effect from 15 th August, 2025. As of June, 2026, more than 77 
lakh Annual Passes have been issued registering 63 crore transactions 

2 
 
on National Highway Fee Plazas. Presently, around 33% of total 
Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) transactions done by car/jeep/van are 
Annual Pass Transactions.  
(c) Fee plazas are established on National Highways as per the 
provisions of the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and 
Collection) Rules, 2008, wherein Sub -Rule (2) of Rule 8, stipulates that 
any other fee plaza on the same section of National Highway and in the 
same direction are not   established within a distance of 60 km. Further 
the proviso to the said Rule also states that where the executing 
authority deems necessary, it may for reasons to be recorded in writing, 
establish or allow to establish another fee plaza within a distance of 60 
km. 
For cases having less inter distance between fee plaza, the location of 
fee plaza  is examined by a Committee  as per the provisions of NH Fee 
Rules 2008,  considering all local factors and other nearby National 
Highways for making a reco mmendation to the competent 
authority regarding publication of fee notification in the Gazette of India 
and the commencement of fee collection. 
(d) The Apex Committee and High -Level Empowered Committee 
consisting of Experts from Industry and Academia, in view of security 
and privacy considerations, breach and overall operational control, have 
recommended further deliberations for satellite -based GNSS tolling 
system.  
However, in order to enhance toll operations and enable seamless 
movement of vehicles, the Government has adopted a phased rollout of 
Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) user fee collection on 4 -lane and above 
National Highways, based on the outco mes and efficacy of the awarded 
projects. Under the MLFF tolling system, gantry -mounted high -
performance Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) readers and 
Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras are used for the 
deduction of user fees through the  existing FASTag system. This 
facilitates barrier -less tolling, wherein user fees are collected from 

3 
 
vehicle users without requiring them to stop, slow down, or remain in a 
designated lane.  
Multi-Lane Free Flow based barrier less tolling using existing FA STag 
(RFID)+ANPR/AI- Technology has been awarded on 17 fee plazas. Out of 
17 awarded fee plazas, 05 fee plazas have already gone Live i.e., 
Choryasi Fee Plaza (Surat, Gujarat); Mundka Fee Plaza (Delhi); Gharaunda 
Fee Plaza (Haryana); Manoharpura Fee Plaza (Rajasthan); Daulatpura Fee 
Plaza (Rajasthan). Additional 104 fee plazas have been identified for 
barrier less tolling mechanism under MLFF.

MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- †2018 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 30/07/2026 
  
IMPLEMENTATION OF DEVELOPMENT SCHEMES IN TRIBAL AREAS 
  
†2018. DR. RAJESH MISHRA: 
            DR. MANNA LAL RAWAT: 
            SMT. ANITA NAGARSINGH CHOUHAN: 
            SHRI BHOJRAJ NAG: 
  
Will the Minister of Tribal Affairs be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government has carried out any assessment of the implementation 
and impact of Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN), 
Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) and other tribal development 
programmes; 
  
(b) if so, the details and the present status of the works approved, completed, funds 
utilized and the tribal families benefitted from the said schemes in Madhya Pradesh 
and Chhattisgarh, district-wise; 
  
(c) the measures taken by the Government to strengthen convergence between 
various Ministries of the Union Government and the State Governments for effective 
implementation of tribal development schemes including schemes related to drinking 
water, roads, power supply, health services, education facilities, mobile and internet 
connectivity and skill-development; 
  
(d) the initiatives taken to strengthen the availability of basic services and livelihood 
opportunities in tribal areas particularly in Chhattisgarh, district-wise; and 
  
(e) whether the Govemment proposes to implement any new scheme or package for 
the overall and sustainable development of remote and tribal dominated villages of 
Madhya Pradesh and if so, the details thereof, district-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
 
(a): NITI Aayog (DMEO) has conducted an Evaluation Study of Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes under Package 9, analysing their performance during the period FY 2020–
21 to FY 2024–25 which covered the following Centrally Sponsored schemes under 
Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana:  

  
1.       Pre-Matric Scholarship 
2.       Post Matric Scholarship for STs 
3.       Support to Tribal Research Institutes 
4.       Development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) 
5.       Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) 
6.       Pradhan Mantri Adi Adrash Gram Yojna – PMAAGY (previously known as 
Special Central Assistance to Tribal Sub-Scheme - SCA to TSS). PMAAGY is 
now revamped and is subsumed under DAJGUA 
7.       Administrative Cost to States / UTs 
  
The Ministry has also undertaken evaluation of the following Central Sector schemes: 
  
1.       Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) 
2.       National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of ST Students 
3.       Scholarship to the ST Students for studies abroad 
4.       Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled 
Tribes 
5.       Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) 
6.       Tribal Research Information, Education, Communication and Events (TRI-
ECE) 
7.       Monitoring, Evaluation, Survey and Social Audit (MESSA) 
8.       Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes 
  
DAJGUA was launched on 2nd October, 2024 and is presently under implementation. 
As the programme is at a relatively mid stage, no separate impact assessment has 
been undertaken so far. However, implementation of the interventions under the 
Abhiyan is being regularly monitored through periodic reviews with concerned 
Ministries/Departments, States/UTs and other stakeholders. 
  
(b), (d) & (e): Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) 
and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA JGUA) comprehensively 
target development of tribal / PVTG population in accordance with the approved 
norms. These abhiyans aim to provide basic facilities to improve socio-economic 
conditions of tribals / PVTGs such as safe housing, clean drinking water and 
improved access to education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, 
electrification of unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities.

development schemes to expedite the progress and achievements.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PMAY-U 
 
NO. 2022 SHRI RADHAKRISHNA: 
 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of houses completed under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - 
Urban (PMAY-U) during each of the last five years along with the details 
of funds allocated, sanctioned, released and utilised, city-wise; 
(b) the number of such houses that have remained unoccupied or locked 
for more than one year after completion, city-wise; 
(c) the reasons cited by beneficiaries or Urban Local Bodies for non -
occupation of such houses where surveyed and if so, the details thereof; 
and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to ensure that completed houses 
are actually occupied by the intended beneficiaries?  
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (d):  Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been 
implementing Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY -U) since 
25.06.2015 to provide all weather pucca houses with basic civic 
amenities to eligible urban beneficiaries across the country.  
 
The scheme has four verticals namely, Beneficiary -led individual house 
construction/enhancements (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership 
(AHP), “In -Situ” Slum Redevelopment (ISSR) and Credit Linked Subsidy 
Scheme (CLSS). 
...2/- 
 

 
-2- 
Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY -
U, MoHUA has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 ‘Housing 
for All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban 
areas across the country to support  1 crore additional eligible 
beneficiaries. The scheme is implemented through four verticals i.e., 
Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership 
(AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS). 
The Scheme Guidelines may be accessed at  https://pmay-
urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/Operational-Guidelines-of-PMAY-U-2.pdf. 
Based on the project proposals submitted by the States/UTs  (Union 
Territories), a total of 127.68 lakh houses under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 
have been sanctioned by the Ministry . Out of which, 121.03 lakh houses 
have been grounded and 99.07 lakh are completed/delivered to the 
beneficiaries across the country as on 13.07.2026.  The progress of the 
scheme can also be accessed on the PMAY -U dashboard 
(https://dashboard.pmay-urban.gov.in). City-wise and year-wise details of 
houses completed during each of the last five years alongwith Central 
assistance sanctioned, released, utilized and the total number of houses 
completed since inception under PMAY -U is at the link:  https://pmay-
urban.gov.in/PHQ/LSUQ-2022.pdf 
 
Under the scheme, houses under BLC vertical are  being constructed by 
the beneficiary themselves. Occupancy of AHP/ISSR houses is an 
important concern raised with States/UTs during review meetings. The 
completion of AHP/ISSR houses and their occupancy is a continuous 
phenomenon. The reasons of unoccupancy vary from project to project 
and state to state. The principal reasons for non- occupancy, as reported 
by States/UTs, include incomplete basic infrastructure; reluctance of 
beneficiaries to relocate away from existing livelihood opportunities and 
social networks; financial constraints in meeting the beneficiary  
contribution and delays in documentation and allotment by the 
implementing agencies. As per the scheme guidelines, it is responsibility 
of States/UTs to provide on-site infrastructure such as internal roads,  
…3/- 

 
-3- 
water supply, sewerage/septage, drainage and external electrification 
from their own resources or through convergence with other schemes.  
 
States/UTs are being continuously advised/motivated to expedite 
allotment, provision of infrastructure and ensure occupancy whenever 
necessary by taking proactive steps.  The Ministry conducts regular 
review meetings with the States/UTs to monitor progress of 
implementation of the scheme and expedite completion & occupancy of 
sanctioned houses within the stipulated timeline.

CAPACITY ENHANCEMENT IN THE FOOD PROCESSING SECTOR 
2024. SMT. SMITA UDAY WAGH: 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government has reviewed the progress made in expansion of food 
processing capacity and promotion of value addition under various schemes of the 
Ministry and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government maintains data on investments facilitated for establishment, 
expansion and modernization of food processing units and if so, the details thereof, 
State-wise and district-wise particularly in Maharashtra including Jalgaon district; 
(c)  whether the Government has undertaken measures to promote value-added food 
products, including millet-based products, fruit and vegetable processing and agro-
processing industries in Maharashtra including Jalgaon district and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d)  whether the Government has assessed the employment generated and support extended 
to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), Farmer Producer Organizations 
(FPOs) and food processing enterprises under these initiatives and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(e)  whether the Government proposes to establish additional food processing infrastructure 
and value-addition facilities in Jalgaon Lok Sabha Constituency and if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
  
(a): In order to ensure overall development of food processing sector, Ministry of Food 
Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been incentivizing setting up/expansion of related 
infrastructure through its two Central Sector Schemes namely Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing 
Industry (PLISFPI) and a Centrally sponsored scheme PM Formalization of Micro Food 
Processing Enterprises (PMFME) across the country. 
MoFPI, through its schemes, is helping strengthening of food processing/ preservation 
infrastructure and thereby reducing gap between production and processing capacity. 
Completed projects under component schemes of PMKSY have resulted in creation of about 
241.55 Lakh Metric Tonnes (LMT) of processing capacity per annum across the country. PLI 
FPI has enabled PLI Beneficiary to procure and install advanced machineries at plant site 
resulting in increase in capacity from 39 LMT per annum (pre-PLI) to 73 LMT per annum (post 
PLI).   

 
(b): Food processing sector has attracted US $ 10.34 billion of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)

product specific skilling.

UJJWAL DISCOM ASSURANCE YOJANA 
 
2025. KM. SUDHA R: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the objectives of the Ujjwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY);  
 
(b) whether the said yojana is mandatory for State Distribution Companies 
(DISCOMs) and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) whether annual hikes in domestic electricity consumption charges are 
mandatory and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(d) the deta ils of the financial revival of DISCOMs since the implementation of 
UDAY, Statewise and year-wise;  
 
(e) whether any State Government or DISCOM has opted not to comply with the 
requirements of UDAY and if so, the details thereof including the financial 
consequences arising therefrom; and  
 
(f) whether all the States have adopted UDAY and if so, the details thereof and if 
not, the list of States that have not implemented the scheme? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (f) :  Ujjwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY) was launched in 2015 with 
an overall objective of operational and financial turnaround of State -owned 
distribution utilities through financial restructuring and efficiency improvements in 
distribution sector. UDAY envisaged States taking over 75% of the outstanding debt 
of the DISCOMs, as on 30.09.2015, by issuing SDL (State Development Loan) Bonds. 
Further, States were to take over future losses of DISCOMs in a graded manner as 
per the scheme guidelines. The scheme was optional and 27 States (except Odisha 
and West Bengal) and 5 UTs (except Delhi and Chandigarh) signed Memorandum of 
Understanding (MoU) under UDAY. 
 
  Under the scheme, total bonds worth Rs 2.34 lakh crore were issued 
for debt takeo ver, and DISCOM losses amounting to Rs 36,378 crore were taken 
over by the States as per the scheme guidelines. State-wise details are enclosed at 
Annexure I & II. 
As a result of participation of DISCOMs under UDAY and various other 
reform measures undertaken thereafter by the Central and State Governments, the 
Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses at national level have reduced 
from 25.72% in FY15 to 15.04% in FY25 while the gap between Average Cost of 
Supply and Average Revenue Realized (ACS-ARR) has narrowed from Rs. 0.58/kWh 
to Rs. 0.06/kWh. These collective efforts have also resulted in distribution utilities, 
on an aggregate basis, achieving a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 2,701 crore in FY25 
for the first time since coming into force of Electricity Act, 2003. State-wise details 
at Annexure-III.
