LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO 2027 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 30/07/2026 
BENEFITS FOR STs IN UNION TERRITORRIES  
2027. Shri Rajkumar Roat: 
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the Scheduled Tribes (ST) population as per Census 2011 in the Union Territories in the country and 
the latest estimated population therein along with the details of benefits being provided to ST 
communities in each UT, UT-wise; 
(b) whether the Government has identified members of tribal communities residing in the UT of Delhi 
for more than fifty years and whether the Government proposes to grant them Scheduled Tribe status 
and include them in the enumeration of Scheduled Tribes in the forthcoming Census and if so, the 
timeline thereof; 
 (c) the existing provisions relating to reservation for Scheduled Tribes residing in the Union Territories 
in political institutions and administrative services; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to provide reservation in political institutions and administrative 
services in the Union Territories on the basis of the Scheduled Tribe population and if so, the details and 
the timeline thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
 (SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
(a) Union Territory-wise Scheduled Tribe (ST) population as per Census,2011: 
  
S. No. UT ST Population(in no.’s) 
1 Jammu & Kashmir 12,75,106 
2 Ladhak 2,18,193 
3 Andaman & Nicobar Islands 28,530 
4 Chandigarh NST 
5 Dadra & Nagar haveli and Daman Diu 1,93,927 
6 Lakshadweep 61,120 
7 Puducherry NST 
8 Delhi NST 
Note:’NST’ means No Notified Scheduled Tribes 
The latest census-based figures of ST population will be available after the release of the next 
population census.  
The Government continues to support the welfare and socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes 
through various schemes and interventions of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. These include Dharti Aaba 
Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) for saturation of infrastructure and basic services in tribal 

villages; Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) for the holistic 
development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs); Eklavya Model Residential Schools 
(EMRS) for providing quality residential education to tribal students; Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, National 
Scholarship for Higher Education, National Fellowship and National Overseas Scholarship Schemes for 
educational support; Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution for bridging critical infrastructure 
gaps in Scheduled Areas and tribal areas; Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organisations for education, health 
and livelihood initiatives; Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM), National Scheduled Tribes 
Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) and Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes 
(VCF-ST) for promoting sustainable livelihoods, entrepreneurship and concessional credit; and Tribal 
Research, Information, Education, Communication and Events (TRI-ECE) for research, documentation 
and capacity building. In addition, health, education, drinking water, connectivity and other 
infrastructure-related interventions are being implemented through convergence with the concerned 
Ministries/Departments. 
(b):       As per available information no proposal for grant of Scheduled Tribe status to any community 
on the basis of duration of residence in the UT of Delhi is under consideration in this Ministry. Grant of 
Scheduled Tribe status is governed by Article 342 of the Constitution, under which a community can be 
specified as a Scheduled Tribe only through a notification issued by the President after consultation with 
the Governor/Administrator concerned, and any subsequent inclusion or exclusion is affected only by an 
Act of Parliament amending the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950. Such proposals are 
examined against the criteria recommended by the Lokur Committee (1965) — namely, indications of 
primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact with the community at 
large, and social and economic backwardness — and require a specific recommendation from the 
concerned State Government/UT Administration, followed by concurrence of the Registrar General of 
India and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes. 
(c) and (d): Reservation for Scheduled Tribes in Union Territories is presently provided as under: 
(i) Political institutions: Reservation of seats for STs in the UT Legislative 
Assemblies/Panchayats/Municipalities is provided in proportion to their population under the respective 
Government of Union Territories Act, 1963, the Delimitation Act, 2002 and other applicable local laws, 
in Union Territories having notified ST population, namely Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, 
and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. No such reservation applies in Chandigarh, Delhi and 
Puducherry, since no ST is notified therein. 
(ii) Administrative services: Reservation in direct recruitment to civil posts and services under the Union 
Territory administrations follows the reservation policy of the Department of Personnel & Training 
(DoPT), Government of India, which prescribes 7.5% reservation for Scheduled Tribes at the all-India 
level. In Union Territories with a predominant or substantial ST population (such as Lakshadweep and 
Dadra & Nagar Haveli), a higher percentage of reservation is provided in local/UT cadre recruitment, 
commensurate with the local ST population, as notified by the respective UT Administration from time 
to time.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2028 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
  
CONSTRUCTION OF HIGHWAYS UNDER BHARATMALA PARIYOJANA 
  
2028.  SHRI ATUL GARG:  
  SHRI ARUN BHARTI:  
  SMT. SHAMBHAVI:  
  DR. D. PURANDESWARI:  
  SHRI RAJESH VERMA: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the pace of highway construction under the Bharatmala 
Pariyojana has successfully transformed  the nation's connectivity, 
drastically reducing travel times for common citizens; 
(b) if so, the access -controlled expressways and national highways 
successfully completed and opened to the public during the last two 
financial years particularly in Ghaziabad & Jamui, Samastipur, 
Rajahmundry and Khagaria Lok Sabha Constituencies; 
(c) whe ther this visionary infrastructure push has seamlessly 
connected isolated rural agricultural hubs to major urban markets, 
directly multiplying the daily incomes of ordinary small - scale 
farmers, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the details of the massive di rect and indirect employment 
opportunities successfully generated for millions of rural youth 
through these mega road construction projects; and 
(e) the future steps planned to build State -of-the-art wayside 
amenities, featuring affordable food courts and clean public 
washrooms, every fifty kilometers for the comfort of common 
travellers? 

ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a)     Yes Sir.   The implementation of project under Bharatmala 
Pariyojana has signific antly strengthened the National Highway 
network by improving connectivity between economic centres, 
ports, industrial clusters, border areas, and tourist destinations. 
Development of access -controlled expressways and high -speed 
corridors under the programm e is envisaged to reduce travel time 
by 40 –50% between key economic centres and major destinations, 
while enhancing logistics efficiency, reducing vehicle operating 
costs, and providing safer and faster travel for commuters. Overall, 
the programme has substantially improved connectivity and mobility 
across the country. 
  
(b)     Total length of National Highways including Access -Controlled 
Highway/Expressway constructed in the Financial Year 2024 -25 and 
2025-26 is 10,660 km and 9,361 km, respectively across  the country 
including Lok Sabha Constituencies of  Ghaziabad & Jamui, 
Samastipur, Rajahmundry and Khagaria.  
  
(c)     The study conducted by Indian Institute of Management (IIM), 
Bangalore to evaluate the impact of Bharatmala Pariyojana 
indicates positive  effects across multiple sectors. Economically, 
household income and expenditure has increased. Logistics 
efficiency has improved with reduced costs. Businesses have 
benefited from better access to markets and factories. Socially, 
travel time to schools an d healthcare facilities has decreased, 
enhancing accessibility. Overall, the study suggests that 
Bharatmala Pariyojana has significantly contributed to socio -
economic growth. 
  
(d)     As per the study by IIT Kanpur, development of each lane -
kilometer of a highway generates about 4,500 person -days of direct 
employment and about 5,600 person -days of indirect employment. 
Accordingly, project under Bharatmala Pariyojana has generated 
huge direct as also indirect employment across the country.  
  
(e)     Government envisions development of wayside amenities, at 
approx. interval of 40 -60 kms along National Highways and 

Expressways for providing public facilities like eateries, toilet, 
drinking water, parking, fuel stations, EV charging stations, short 
term a ccommodation, medical aid etc. to the road users and 
truckers. 
  
As on date, 137 WSA sites are operational along National 
Highways and Expressways across the country.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2029 
TO BE ANSWERED ON JULY 30, 2026 
 
INCREASING DEMAND FOR AFFORDABLE HOUSING  
 
NO. 2029 DR. KIRSAN NAMDEO: 
Will the Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that rapid urbanisation has 
resulted in increasing demand for affordable housing, basic civic 
amenities and sustainable urban infrastructure across the country; 
(b) if so, the details of the various schemes and programmes being 
implemented by the Government for providing affordable housing, 
improving urban infrastructure and ensuring better living 
conditions for urban citizens during the last five years; 
(c) the details of the funds allocated, sanctioned and utilised under 
such schemes, State-wise including Maharashtra; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the shortage of affordable 
housing and gaps in urban infrastructure in smaller towns, 
aspirational districts and tribal -dominated areas and if  so, the 
details thereof; and 
(e) the corrective measures being taken to address these challenges? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (e): Rapid Urbanization results in increasing demands for 
affordable housing, basic civic amenities, water and sustainable urban 
infrastructure. The rapid growth of urban areas due to increasing 
economic activities, employment opportunities and migration has 
necessitated planned urban development with adequate housing and 
infrastructure facilities.  Land’ and ‘Colonisation’ are State subjects. 
Therefore, schemes related to housing, water, other basic civic 
amenities and sustainable urban infrastructure for their citizens are 
implemented by States/Union Territories (UTs) in their respective 
areas.  
 
…2/- 
 

-2- 
However, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) supplements 
the efforts of States/UTs, including the State of Maharashtra, through 
various Missions, such as Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-
U) & PMAY -U 2.0, Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban (SBM-U) & SBM -U 
2.0, Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 
& AMRUT 2.0, Metro Rail Projects, PM -eBus Sewa Scheme, Urban 
Challenge Fund (UCF) etc. 
 
MoHUA has been implementing PMAY -U since 25.06.2015 to provide 
all weather pucca houses with basic civic amenities to eligible urban 
beneficiaries across the country  including the State of Maharashtra. 
Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of 
PMAY-U, MoHUA has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY-U 2.0 
‘Housing for All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for 
implementation in urban areas across the country to support 1 crore 
additional eligible beneficiaries  including beneficiaries from smaller 
towns, aspirational districts and tribal-dominated areas.  
 
PMAY-U & PMAY-U 2.0 adopts a demand driven approach and no target 
has been fixed by the Government. States/UTs assess the requirement 
through their Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/Implementing Agencies in 
their respective jurisdictions. Eligible citizens apply t hrough Unified 
Web Portal of PMAY -U 2.0 with all details on the portal. 
States/UTs/ULBs validate the beneficiaries as per the eligibility 
criteria of the scheme guidelines and selection/scrutiny of beneficiary 
lists are done by the States/UTs. The Scheme G uidelines and Unified 
Web Portal for submitting the online applications can be accessed 
through https://pmay-urban.gov.in. 
 
Under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, a total of 127.68 lakh houses including 
16.20 lakh under PMAY-U 2.0 have been sanctioned by the Ministry, so 
far. Out of which, 121.03 lakh houses have been grounded and 99.07 
lakh are completed/ delivered to the beneficiaries across the country 
as on 13.07.2026. A total of ₹2,12,483 crore of Central Assistance has 
been approved of which ₹1,80,582 crore has been released to 
States/UTs based on the compliances submitted by them. State/UT -
wise detail of the Central Assistance sanctioned, released and utilized 
during the last five years and since inception are enclosed at 
Annexure.  
…3/- 

-3- 
Under SBM -U funds were provided to States/UTs, inter alia, for 
constructing Community/Public Toilets (CT/PTs) and Individual 
Household Latrines (IHHLs). CTs and IHHLs primarily serve 
underprivileged households, while PTs cater to the general public and 
floating population.  Further, SBM -U 2.0 has been launched on 1st 
October 2021 in all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/cities, with objective of 
attaining 100% Garbage Free Cities (GFC). Central Assistance is 
provided for setting up various types of waste processing facilities, 
Used Water Management and Toilets components as well as 
Information Education Communication (IEC) and Capacity Building 
activities.   
 
Under SBM -U 2.0, central assistance of ₹36,465 crore has been 
allocated, of which ₹9,205 crore has been released to States/UTs  
including ₹ 1,079 crore in the State of Maharashtra as on date.  
 
The Government of India launched the AMRUT in June 2015 to ensure 
basic urban infrastructure in selected 500 cities of the country with 
focus on water supply, sewerage and septage management, storm 
water drainage, non- motorized urban transport and development of 
green spaces. Further, AMRUT 2.0 scheme has been launched on 1st 
October 2021 in all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/cities, enabling the 
cities to become 'self -reliant' and 'water secure'. Under AMRUT, 
States/UTs have taken up 6,007 projects worth ₹83,491 crore. A  total 
₹34,901 crore have been released to States/UTs for the projects 
including ₹ 3,356 crore in Maharashtra, of which ₹33,444 crore has 
been utilised. Under AMRUT 2.0,  a total of ₹ 23,752  crore has been 
released/ Mother Sanction issued to the States/ UTs for projects under 
AMRUT 2.0 including ₹ 3,760 crore in Maharashtra, of which ₹19,942 
crore has been utilized. 
 
MoHUA has notified various guiding documents to help 
cities/ULBs/States/UTs regarding urban transport . Apart from policy 
initiatives, at present about 1,159 kms of Metro Rail Network 
(including 82.15 km of RRTS) is operational in 26 cities of the country. 
Also, PM-eBus Sewa Scheme was launched on 16th August 2023 with 
an aim to augment bus operations in urban areas with deployment of 
10,000 electric buses for 116 cities across 26 States/UTs . As on 
10.07.2026, more than 200 infrastructure projects in 100+ cities  
…4/- 

-4- 
(Behind-the-Meter Power & Civil Infrastructure) have been sanctioned 
amounting to ₹1352 crore including ₹373 crore for the State of  
Maharashtra.  Apart from this, bus Operational Subsidy of ₹11.79 crore 
have also been released for 4 cities including ₹2.67 crore for Nagpur 
(Maharashtra).  
 
The Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) scheme has been operationalized 
since 15th April, 2026. UCF supports the development and 
strengthening of urban infrastructure through implementation of 
transformative and impactful projects under three verticals namely 
Cities as Growth Hubs, Creative Redevelopment of Cities and Water 
and Sanitation. So far, 33 projects have been approved/ accorded in-
principle approval including 3 projects from the state of Maharashtra 
with total project cost of ₹1983 crore and Central assistance of ₹478 
crore.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2030 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
 
SETTING UP OF PUMPED STORAGE PROJECTS IN MADHYA PRADESH 
 
†2030. SHRI BUNTY VIVEK SAHU: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has made any assessment of the possibilities of 
setting up of Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) in the Chhindwara district of 
Madhya Pradesh f or the integration of renewable energy and management of 
peak electricity demand keeping in view its geographical suitability and if so, 
the details thereof;  
 
(b) whether any special positive steps are taken in collaboration with the private 
and public sectors to encourage the establishment of such projects to promote 
green energy through proper utilization of water resources in the district and if 
so, the details thereof; and  
 
(c) the budgetary or technical assistance being provided by the Government for 
the speedy implementation of proposed PSPs in the State including 
Chhindwara? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a): As per information available in Central Electricity Authority (CEA), one 
Pumped Storage Project (PSP) namely Satpura-2 with installed capacity of 1000 
MW has been identified in Chhindwara, Madhya Pradesh. 
 
(b):    The Government has taken several policy measures to promote the 
development of Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) across the country, including 
in Madhya Pradesh, through participation of Central and State Public Sector 
Undertakings as well as private developers. These measures include:  
 
(i) Ministry of Power has notified guidelines to promote development of 
Pumped Storage Projects in the country on 10.04.2023.  
 
(ii) To provide a transparent, fair, standardized procurement framework based 
on open competitive bidding with appropriate risk-sharing between various 
stakeholders, MoP vide Gazette notification dated 06.02.2025, has notified 
tariff based competitive bidding (T BCB) guidelines for procurement of 
storage capacity/stored energy from pumped storage plants.  
 
(iii) Budgetary Support towards Cost of Enabling Infrastructure, i.e., 
roads/bridges, railway sidings, ropeways, communication infrastructure 
and transmission line from power house to nearest pooling point. 

 
(iv) The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC), vide its Notification 
dated 26.06.2025, has provided for 100% waiver of Inter -State 
Transmission System (ISTS) charges for Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) 
for a period of 25 years from the Commercial Operat ion Date (COD), in 
respect of projects for which the construction work is awarded on or before 
30.06.2028. 
 
(v) The Government of India, vide Gazette notification dated 01.08.2025, has 
revised the capital expenditure limit for schemes related to setting up 
hydro generating stations to ₹3,000 crore, requiring the concurrence of the 
CEA. Further, the Government has exempted off -stream closed -loop 
pumped storage schemes, irrespective of the quantum of capital 
expenditure, from the requirement of concurrence by the CEA. 
 
(vi) Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has revised Guidelines for formulation 
and concurrence of Detailed Project Report (DPR) of PSPs. Under the 
revised guidelines, the timeline for concurrence of DPR has been reduced 
from 90 days to 50 days for PSPs.  Further, the clearance of Inter -State 
Aspects is not required for PSPs. 
 
(vii) Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC), vide its 
notification dated 18.05.2023, has enabled appraisal of PSPs under B2 
category subject to certain conditions.   
 
(viii) The MoEF&CC on 14.08.2023, has issued specific Terms of Reference (TOR) 
for the proposals involving off stream PSPs wherein collection of baseline 
data for one season (other than monsoon) is prescribed for off stream 
closed loop PSPs and collection of base line data for two seasons (pre -
monsoon & post-monsoon) is prescribed for off stream open loop PSPs. 
 
(ix) The MOEF&CC on 20.08.2024, has extended the provisions relating to 
survey in the forest areas for mining projects to other development projects 
including hydel/PSPs.  
 
(x) MOEF&CC vide letter dated 10.09.2025  has enhanced the number of 
boreholes for undertaking survey and explorations in the forest area for 
mining and developmental projects including hydel / PSPs. 
 
(c) :  The Government facilitates the timely implementation of Pumped Storage 
Projects (PSPs), including those in Madhya Pradesh, by providing technical 
support through the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), including appraisal of 
Detailed Project Reports (DPRs ), issuance of technical guidelines and 
monitoring of project implementation. In addition, the Government provides 
Budgetary Support, under the Scheme, to eligible PSPs towards the cost of 
enabling infrastructure, including roads and bridges, railway sidings, ropeways, 
communication infrastructure, and the transmission line from the powerhouse 
to the nearest pooling point.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 2031 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 30/07/2026 
  
STATUS OF PM-JANMAN 
  
2031. SHRI PRADEEP PUROHIT: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government has implemented the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha 
Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) for the socio-economic development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal 
Groups (PVTGs) and if so, the objectives, eligibility criteria and major components thereof; 
(b) the details of PVTG habitations in the State of Odisha, along with the number of eligible and 
covered beneficiaries under PM-JANMAN, district-wise and block-wise; 
(c) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under PM-JANMAN in Odisha since the 
launch of the Scheme along with the details of Central assistance provided to the State, district 
wise; 
(d) the details of physical achievements under the Scheme in Odisha, including houses, roads, 
drinking water facilities, mobile connectivity, hostels and other infrastructure created for PVTGs, 
district-wise; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to expand coverage to all eligible PVTG habitations in the 
State and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
  
(a), (b) & (e): Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha AbhiyaN (PM JANMAN) was 
launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on 15th November, 2023 for the socio-economic 
development of the 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) communities residing in 18 
States and one Union Territory. The mission aims to provide basic facilities to improve their socio-
economic conditions such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, 
health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified households and 
sustainable livelihood opportunities. These objectives are being met through 11 interventions 
implemented by 9-line Ministries.  
  
Ministry of Tribal Affairs through the State Governments/ UT Administration/departments has

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2032 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
 
PROGRESS MADE UNDER RDSS 
 
2032. SHRI YADUVEER WADIYAR: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the progress made under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) 
in reducing Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses across the 
country;  
 
(b) the targets fixed under the said scheme for reduction of AT&C losses and 
the current achievement levels, State-wise including Karnataka;  
 
(c) the funds sanctioned and released under RDSS to Karnataka for feeder 
separation, smart metering and infrastructure strengthening; and  
 
(d) the measurable impact of RDSS interventions on improving operational 
efficiency and financial sustainability of DISCOMs? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (d): Government of India (GoI) launched the Revamped Distribution 
Sector Scheme (RDSS) in July 2021 with the objective of improving the 
quality and reliability of power supply to consumers through a financially 
sustainable and operationally efficient dist ribution sector. The Scheme 
has an outlay of Rs. 3,03,758 crore with an estimated Central Grant of Rs. 
97,631 crore. The Scheme aims at reducing the Aggregate Technical and 
Commercial (AT&C) losses to pan-India levels of 12-15%. 
Under the Scheme, financial  assistance is being provided to the 
distribution utilities (excluding private sector utilities) for undertaking 
loss reduction infrastructure works and smart metering works. Projects 
worth Rs. 1.53 lakh crore for loss reduction infrastructure works and Rs. 
1.31 lakh crore for smart metering works have been sanctioned under the 
Scheme. 

The following works have been sanctioned under the Scheme to 
strengthen the distribution network and reduce AT&C losses: 
 
 Creation of new substations and upgradation of exist ing 
substations. 
 Installation of new Distribution Transformers (DTs) and 
augmentation of existing DTs. 
 Replacement of old conductors. 
 Agriculture feeder segregation works. 
 IT/OT systems like Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition 
(SCADA) to improve grid monitoring. 
 Smart metering works covering 19.79 crore consumers, 2.11 lakh 
feeders and 52.53 lakh DTs. Smart metering works help in improving 
the billing efficiency of utilities through automated energy 
accounting, which enables identification of leakages and high-loss 
areas, and in improving the collection efficiency of utilities through 
the pre-paid system. 
The release of funds under the Scheme is contingent upon 
improvement in the operational and financial performance of the 
distribution utilities. This, in addition to other initiatives taken by GoI, has 
helped in bringing discipline in the payment of Government subsidies and 
Government department dues to the utilities, regular issuance of tariff 
orders, publishing of accounts, non-creation of regulatory assets, etc. 
With the concerted efforts of the Central and State Governments 
and as a result of the reform measures undertaken, AT&C losses across 
the country have reduced from 21.91% in FY21 to 15.04% in FY25. 
Further, the gap between the Average Cost of Supply (ACS) and the 
Average Revenue Realised (ARR) has reduced from Rs. 0.69/kWh in FY21 
to Rs. 0.06/kWh in FY25. Distribution Utility wise details of AT&C losses 
and targets prescribed under RDSS are enclosed in Annexure. 
As regards Karnataka, the State has not availed assistance under 
RDSS for loss reduction and smart metering works. However, household 
electrification works worth Rs. 45 crore (GBS: 27 crore), covering 
electrification of 6,903 households, have been sanctioned for Karnataka, 
as per the proposal submitted by the State. Out of this, 3,260 households 
have been electrified and Rs 10.14 crore have been released, till date.

Domestic LPG Prices 
 
2033. SHRI RAJEEV RAI: 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has recently reduced the price of commercial LPG cylinders by 
about one hundred and eighty-three rupees per cylinder and has left domestic LPG refill 
prices unchanged, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the international crude oil prices have declined to levels prevailing prior to the 
recent geopolitical conflict in West Asia; 
(c) if so, the quarter-wise details of crude oil prices at which India purchased crude oil from 
the international market during the last two years; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to review domestic LPG prices in view of the easing of 
international crude oil prices, if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुर ेश गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (d): Prices of LPG in the country are linked to Saudi CP, the benchmark for LPG 
prices in international market. Government continues to review and modulate the effective 
price to consumer for domestic LPG only.  
With the onset of the West Asia crisis, the average Saudi CP (the international benchmark for 
LPG pricing) rose upto US$ 780/MT in April and May 2026. In June 2026, as the Saudi CP 
rose further to US$ 796/MT (excluding premium), the Market Determined Price (MDP) of a 
14.2 kg domestic LPG cylinder went to Rs.1,695 per 14.2 Kg cylinder.  
The Retail Selling Price (RSP) of domestic LPG has been maintained at Rs. 942 per 14.2 kg 
cylinder. At this price, there is an implicit subsidy (under-recovery) of over Rs. 500 per 14.2 
kg cylinder as of July 2026; the corresponding under-recovery exceeded Rs. 700 per 14.2 kg 
cylinder in June 2026. For more than 10.5 crore PMUY consumers, the effective price is only 
Rs. 642 per cylinder (Delhi), after a targeted subsidy of Rs. 300 per cylinder, in addition to 
the implicit subsidy of more than Rs 500 per cylinder. 
On the other hand, Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (PSU OMCs) and private sector 
LPG marketing companies are free to determine the prices of commercial LPG based on 
prevailing international market prices and market conditions. Accordingly, the Retail Selling 
Price of 19 kg commercial LPG cylinders is revised and declared by the OMCs on a monthly 
basis, without any Government intervention. The Retail Selling Price (RSP) of a 19 kg 
commercial LPG cylinder was  revised in June 2026 to Rs. 2,930.00 by the Oil Marketing 
Companies in July 2026. 
Even the crude oil prices were USD 69/barrel in February 2026 prior to the crisis and 
continue to remain high (USD 103.33/barrel on 23rd July 2026). The quarter-wise details of 
crude oil imported and its value since April 2024 are given at Annexure.

SMT. BHARTI PARDHI:  
SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of housing targets set and funds sanctioned for 
Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh during the current financial year under 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U) keeping in view the acute 
housing shortage;  
(b) whether the Union Government proposes to grant any special 
concessions or land transfer approvals to the State Governments for 
redevelopment of slums situated on Railway, Port Trust or other Central 
Government lands in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh and if so, the 
details thereof;  
(c) the number of proposals pending with the Union Government for 
providing permanent housing to slum dwellers on Central lands in 
Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh through the In- Situ Slum 
Redevelopment (ISSR) component under PMAY-U;  
(d) the details of any new Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) being 
implemented to provide interest subvention on home loans for Middle 
and Low -Income Group (MIG/LIG) families in Maharashtra and Madhya 
Pradesh; and  
(e) the specific policy guidelines issued by the Ministry to facilitate 
utilisation of Union Government lands for mega redevelopment projects? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
 MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (e): ‘Land’ and ‘Colonization’ are State subjects. Therefore, 
schemes related to housing for their citizens are implemented by  
                                                                            
…2/-

States/Union Territories (UTs) in their respective areas. However, Ministry 
of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) supplements the efforts of 
States/UTs by providing Central Assistance under Pradhan Mantri Awas 
Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U) since June 25, 2015 to provide pucca houses to 
all eligible urban beneficiaries across the country  including Maharashtra 
and Madhya Pradesh. 
Based on the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY-U, 
MoHUA has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 ‘Housing for 
All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban areas 
across the country  including Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh to support 
1 crore additional eligible beneficiaries  including Low Income Group (LIG)  
and Middle Income Group (MIG)  categories. PMAY-U 2.0 is implemented 
through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable 
Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and 
Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS).  
The ISS vertical is implemented as a Central Sector Scheme through 
Central Nodal Agencies such as National Housing Bank (NHB), State Bank 
of India (SBI) and Housing and Urban Development Corporation Ltd. 
(HUDCO). Prospective beneficiaries can apply on unified web portal 
available at  https://pmay-urban.gov.in. As per the scheme guidelines of 
PMAY-U 2.0, under ISS vertical, a maximum release of interest subsidy of 
₹1.80 lakh is provided to eligible beneficiaries in five yearly installments.  
PMAY-U and PMAY -U 2.0 adopt  a demand driven approach wherein 
States/Union Territories (UTs) assess the requirement through their Urban 
Local Bodies (ULBs)/Implementing Agencies in their respective 
jurisdictions. Eligible citizens are also allowed to apply through Unified 
Web Portal of PMAY -U 2.0 with all details on the portal. States/UTs/ULBs 
validate the beneficiaries as per the eligibility criteria of the scheme 
guidelines and selection/scrutiny of beneficiary lists are done by the 
States/UTs. The Scheme Guidelines and Unified Web Portal for submitting 
the online applications can be accessed through https://pmay-urban.gov.in.  
...3/- 
 

-3- 
As per scheme guidelines, Central Government land owning agencies could 
also undertake “in- situ” slum redevelopment on their lands occupied by 
slum dwellers under PMAY -U 2.0. Land owning agencies have their own 
policies of land management and States/UTs may coordinate with such 
agencies for relocation/redevelopment of slums on such land. 
Based on the demand survey and selection of beneficiaries, the project 
proposals are prepared and approved by the State Level Sanctioning and 
Monitoring Committee (SLSMC) headed by the Chief Secretary of 
States/UTs for further consideration of release of Central Assistance by 
the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC).   
Based on the project proposal submitted by Maharashtra and Madhya 
Pradesh 13.84 lakh and 10.39 lakh houses respectively have been 
sanctioned under PMAY-U/PMAY-U 2.0 so far, of which 10.74 lakh and 9.10 
lakh houses have been completed/delivered. D uring the current financial 
year 30,945 and 27,361 houses have been sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0 
and central assistance of ₹351.03 crore and ₹376.01 crore have been 
released in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh respectively.  The progress 
of the scheme can also be accessed on the PMAY -U dashboard 
(https://dashboard.pmay-urban.gov.in). 
A total of 10,848 and 38,339 beneficiaries have availed benefits under the 
ISS vertical of PMAY -U 2.0 in the States of Madhya Pradesh and 
Maharashtra respectively.  No project proposal related to slum 
redevelopment for Union Government owned land in Maharashtra and 
Madhya Pradesh is pending under PMAY-U/ PMAY-U 2.0 in the Ministry.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2035 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
 
ASSESSMENT OF NATIONAL POWER GRID 
 
2035. SHRI JAI PRAKASH: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any comprehensive assessmen t 
of the preparedness of the National Power Grid to meet the rapidly growing 
electricity demand arising from renewable energy integration, electric mobility, 
data centres and industrial expansion across  the country and if so, the details 
thereof;  
 
(b) th e details of transmission capacity augmentation, grid modernization, 
deployment of smart grid technologies, battery energy storage systems and 
cyber security measures initiated during the last three years, State -wise and 
project-wise; and  
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to formulate a long term National Grid 
Resilience Strategy to ensure uninterrupted, secure and affordable power 
supply while addressing climate related risks, cyber threats and peak demand 
fluctuations and if so, the details thereof? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) :  To strengthen the transmission infrastructure in line with the growing 
electricity demand, the Government of India notified the National Electricity 
Plan (Volume -II: Transmission) in 2024. The plan outlines the transmission 
system requirements for the period 2023 –2032, commensurate with the 
projected generation capacity additions and anticipated growth in electricity 
demand across various emerging and conventional sec tors of the economy 
(including electric mobility, data centres and industrial expansion across the 
country). The transmission planning also takes into account evolving load 
centres and new categories of electricity demand, while ensuring reliable 
integration of renewable energy.  
 
The transmission plan includes the addition of central and state 
transmission systems to meet the projected peak electricity demand of 388 GW 
by 2032. As per the plan, the transmission network is likely to expand from 5.09 
lakh ck m (as on June, 2026) to 6.48 lakh ckm by 2032 and transformation 
capacity from 1,478 GVA (as on June, 2026) to 2,345 GVA. Also, the inter -
regional transmission capacity is planned to increase from 120 GW (as on June, 
2026) to 168 GW by the year 2032. 
 

 
 
 
(b):    The details of transmission capacity augmentation, grid modernization, 
deployment of smart grid technologies, battery energy storage systems and 
cyber security measures initiated during the last three years are as follows: 
 
1. Details of Transmission capacity augmentation: 
 
A total of 35,172 circuit km of transmission lines and 270,174 MVA of 
transformation capacity (220 kV and above) have been added during the last 
three years (FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26). Summary of the transmission lines and 
transformation capacity augmented is given at Annexure-I. 
 
2. Grid Modernization and deployment of smart grid technologies: 
 
 Advanced grid support technologies such as Static Synchronous 
Compensators (STATCOMs), Synchronous Condensers (SynCONs), and other 
Flexible AC Tra nsmission System (FACTS) devices are being deployed to 
enhance voltage stability, improve system strength, and support reliable 
integration of renewable energy. Further, several measures have been taken  
to facilitate renewable energy integration, including establishment of Regional 
Energy Management Centres (REMCs) for renewable forecasting and real-time 
grid management, implementation of Automatic Generation Control (AGC) and 
Ancillary Services (SRAS/TRAS) for frequency regulation and balancing etc. 
 
3. Battery energy storage system (BESS): 
 
As on 30.06.2026, the installed capacity of Battery Energy Storage 
Systems (BESS) with capacity greater than 1 MWh is 2,927.85 MW / 8,660.20 
MWh in the country. State wise details are given at Annexure-II. 
 
4.  Cyber security measures: 
 
To strengthen the cyber security of Indian electricity grid, the 
Government of India has established a sector specific cyber security 
incident response team, namely, Computer Security Incident Response Team 
– Power (CSIRT -Power) in April, 2023  for coordinating, reporting, and 
responding to cyber security incidents in power sector. Cyber security 
measures undertaken during the last three years include approval of funding 
under Power System Development Fund (PSDF) for establishment of a 
Security Operations Centre (SOC) and a Network Operations Centre (NOC) to 
strengthen cyber security monitoring and incident response.  
 
Further, cyber security training programmes, workshops and capacity -
building initiatives are being organized regularly in collabo ration with the 
Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), 
the National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC) 
and other institutions to enhance cyber security awareness and capabilities 
across the power sector.  
 
 
 

(c) : The Government has already initiated several measures to enhance the 
resilience, reliability and security of the national grid. In this regard, Task Force 
on Cyclone Resilient Robust Electricity Transmission and Distribution 
Infrastructure in Coastal Areas has recommended a comprehensive set of 
measures including, enhanced transmission planning based on higher 
contingency criteria, Critical Infrastructure Protection Framework, Mapping of 
Transmission and Distribution (T&D) infrastructure in cyclone affected zones, 
Designing of Distribution network in Ring or Mesh configuration, emergency 
restoration systems, Mobile substations, Mobile DGs set, digitalisation of 
power system assets, deployment of distributed energy resources, 
Standardization and use of Energy efficient equipment, use of advanced 
technologies such as Unmanned Arial Vehicles (UAVs) / Drones for inspection 
and monitoring, Underground transmission corridor along coastal highway 
project etc.  
 
Cyber resilience of the National G rid is being strengthened through 
round-the-clock (RTC) monitoring through the Security Operations Centre (SOC) 
and Network Operations Centre (NOC) at CSIRT -Power and GRID -INDIA; the 
system has also continuously been monitored by CERT-IN and National Critical 
Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC). Periodic Vulnerability 
Assessment and Penetration Testing (VA/PT) of Information Technology (IT) 
and Operational Technology (OT) infrastructure, and continuous capacity 
building in collaboration wi th reputed technical and national security 
institutions, so that preparedness keeps pace with the evolving cyber threat 
landscape.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2038 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
 
REVIV AL OF VILLAGE AND COTTAGE INDUSTRIES  
 
2038.   SHRI RAJU BISTA: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total financial assistance provided to small businesses under the Prime Minister’s Employment 
Generation Programme (PMEGP) and other Credit schemes in Darjeeling and Kalimpong districts during 
the last five years; 
(b)  the steps taken to upgrade the processing, packaging and marketing of local products, including 
orthodox tea, ginger, cardamom and traditional handicrafts; and 
(c)  the steps being taken by the Ministry to revive and modernize traditional village and cottage 
industries in rural areas to prevent youth migration and generate sustainable local employment? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a): Details on financial assistance provided to small businesses under the Prime Minister ’s 
Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) and other Credit schemes in Darjeeling and Kalimpong 
districts during the last five years is provided below: 
i. Under PMEGP, Margin Money (MM) Subsidy amounting to Rs. 6.56 crore in Darjeeling district 
and Rs. 1.97 crore in Kalimpong district has been disbursed during the last five years. 
ii. Under National SC -ST Hub scheme of the Ministr y of MSME, capital subsidy amounting to Rs. 
18.2 lakh has been released in Darjeeling district during the last five years.  
iii. Under the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme, 
subsidy amounting to Rs. 66.49 lakh in Darjeeling district and Rs. 6.61 lakh in Kalimpong di strict 
has been provided during the last five years. 
 
(b):  Steps taken for upgradation of processing, packaging and marketing of local products  including 
orthodox tea, ginger, cardamom and traditional handicrafts include the following: 
i. Under the Procureme nt and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme, financial assistance is provided to 
eligible Micro and Small Enterprises for participation in domestic trade fairs/exhibitions , Vendor 
Development Programmes, National Workshops/Seminars, barcode registration and adoption of e -
commerce platforms i.e. MSME Global Mart  to strengthen the marketing and enhance market 
access of MSE products including orthodox tea, ginger, cardamom and traditional handicrafts. 
ii. Micro and small enterprises have bee n registered under the MSME TEAM (Trade Enablement and 
Marketing) initiative to expand market reach and strengthen digital credibility by onboarding them 
onto Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC). 
iii. Marketing support is provided to registered producers through Khadi and Village Industries 
Commission (KVIC) Sales outlets. Furthermore, Exhibitions and Workshops are arranged regularly 
for participation of beneficiaries of KVI sector. 
iv. E‑commerce portal (https://www.ekhadiindia.com) has been developed to provi de a digital 
marketplace for global product sales and to promote Khadi and Village Industries products. 

: 2 : 
 
 
v. To promote V ocal for Local Initiative in food processing sector, PMFME Scheme primarily adopts 
One District One Product (ODOP) approach to selec t, brand, and promote at least One Product 
from each District of the country for enabling holistic socio  economic growth across all regions. 
The Scheme provides financial, technical and business support for upgradation of micro food 
processing enterprises engaged in processing of all the products, including ort hodox tea, ginger and 
cardamom and supports technology upgradation, common infrastructure, branding & marketing, 
packaging, quality standardisation, food safety compliance and market linkages.  
 
(c) Steps being taken by the Ministry through various schemes to revive and modernize traditional 
village and cottage industries prevent ing youth migration and generating  sustainable local employment 
opportunities include the following: 
I. Under PMEGP: 
i. Around 80% of the total units assisted under PMEGP during the last five years have been 
assisted in rural areas.  
ii. Enhancement of maximum project cost from Rs. 25 lakh to Rs. 50 lakh for manufacturing sector 
and from Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 20 lakh for service sector. 
iii. Inclusion of applicants from Aspirational districts and transgenders under Special Category 
eligible for higher subsidy. 
iv. Establishment of PMEGP Helpdesks at State Offices to provide real -time assistance and hand -
holding to potential beneficiaries. 
v. A wide range of more than 1,000 Model of Detailed Project Reports prepared on various 
industries have been made available on the PMEGP portal. 
vi. Disseminating Information, Education and Communication (IEC) material and video clips in 
regional languages for promotion in remote areas. 
vii. As per RBI Master Directions on lending to MSMEs, no collateral security to be insisted by 
Banks for projects involving loan up to Rs. 20 lakh. Strict compliance of this provision has been 
reemphasized to all financing Banks. 
viii. Periodical review meetings by the Ministry with Implementing Agencies i.e. KVIC, State offices 
of KVIC, State Khadi and Village Industries Boards (KVIBs), State District Industries Centres 
(DICs) and financial institutions. 
ix. Awareness and outreach programmes in all the States/UTs including backward and under - 
performing areas, Aspirational districts, NER etc. to identify potential beneficiaries and provide 
handholding support during the application process. 
x. Financial literacy camps and customer awareness programm es conducted by Banks to educate 
prospective entrepreneurs about various initiatives of the Government, including PMEGP. 
 
II. The Ministry also provides credit, skilling and toolkit support through PM Vishwakarma scheme to 
artisans and craftspeople of 18 tradi tional trades, namely: Carpenter, Boat Maker, Armourer, Metal 
Artisan, Tool Kit Maker, Locksmith, Goldsmith, Potter, Sculptor/Stone Worker, Cobbler/Footwear 
Artisan, Mason, Basket/Mat/Broom Maker, Toy Maker (Traditional), Barber, Garland Maker, 
Washerman, Tailor and Fishing Net Maker. 
III. Additionally, KVIC imparts skill development training to unemployed youth under various disciplines 
i.e. Khadi Spinning and Weaving, bakery product, beauty parlour, decorative items, manufacturing of 
Soap and Detergents, Bee-keeping, Stitching, embroidery, Agarbatti making, candle making, Teracotta 
products making, kulhad making, processing of pulses, Achar making, Papad making etc. Selected 
entrepreneurs and artisans engaged in production of unique and quality products are als o provided 
with financial assistance to participate in international exhibitions.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †2039 
ANSWERED ON 30/07/2026 
 
WORK ORDERS FOR JJM IN SIKAR AND JHUNJHUNU DISTRICTS 
 
†2039. SHRI AMRA RAM: 
Will the Minister of Jal Shakti be pleased to state: 
(a) the time by which the work orders under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) for Sikar and Jhunjhunu districts 
are likely to be issued and the time by which the said works are likely to be completed; and 
(b) the details of the approvals accorded so far under JJM in Sikar district, the expected date of completion of 
the works, the number of works completed and the number of works remaining incomplete as on date alo ng 
with the time by which the incomplete works are likely to be completed? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
  
(a) & (b) ‘Drinking Water’ is a state subject, and hence, the responsibility of planning, approval, 
implementation, operation and maintenance (O&M) of drinking water supply schemes, including those under 
the JJM, lies with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supports the states including Rajasthan 
by providing technical and financial assistance.  
To make provision of tap water supply to every rural household across the country, including those in Sikar 
and Jhunjhunu districts of Rajasthan, Government of India, in partnership with States, has been implementing 
Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), since August 2019. 
At the time of announcement of JJM, around 43,600 (11.4%) rural households were reported to have tap water 
connections in Sikar district. So far, as reported by State as on 18.07.2026, around 2.10 lakh additional rural 
households have been provided with tap water  connections. Thus, as on 18.07.2026, out of 3.83 lakh rural 
households, in the district, around 2.53 lakh (66%) households are reported to have tap water supply in their 
homes.  
Similarly, at the start of the Mission, around 60,000 (17.2%) rural households were reported to have tap water 
connections in Jhunjhunu district of Rajasthan. So far, as reported by the State as on 18.07.2026, around 1.29 
lakh additional rural households have been provided with tap water connections under JJM. Thus, as on 
18.07.2026, out of 3.47 lakh rural households in the district, around 1.89 lakh (54.3%) households are reported 
to have tap water supply in their homes. 
As Water is a State subject, project -wise details, inter alia including issuance of work orders of individual 
projects for rural water supply are maintained at the level of State Government.  
Government has approved the extension of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) period up to December 2028 with 
enhanced outlay and restructured implementation focusing on structural reforms in rural drinking water supply 
sector under JJM 2.0.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2041 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 30th July, 2026 
ETHANOL BLENDING AND ITS PRODUCTION COST 
 
2041. DR. T SUMATHY ALIAS THAMIZHACHI THANGAPANDIAN: 
 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Union Government has taken serious note of the adverse effects of ethanol 
blending and the escalation in its cost, if so, the details thereof; and 
(b)  whether it is true that the cost of production of one litre of petrol is lower than the cost of 
production of one litre of ethanol, if so, the details thereof along with the valid reasons for 
the Government to promote ethanol-blended petrol for vehicles and to adhere to the Ethanol 
Blended Petrol Programme? 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏय मंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) & (b): The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a 
phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile 
manufacturers, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Automotive Research Association of India 
(ARAI), Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) 
and other technical institutions. 
Ethanol is not a new fuel. It has been used globally for over a century, with countries such as Brazil 
operating higher ethanol blends for decades. In India, the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme 
commenced with a pilot in 2001, E5 was introduced in 2006, and although blending remained 
around 1.53% in 2013-14, it has since been increased progressively in a calibrated manner after 
creating the necessary production capacity, infrastructure and regulatory framework. 
 
The rollout of higher ethanol blends was undertaken only after extensive consultation with 
automobile manufacturers, SIAM, ARAI, component manufacturers, testing agencies and Oil 
Marketing Companies (OMCs). Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, 
SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile manufacturers covering parameters such as engine durability, 
drivability, startability, corrosion resistance, material compatibility, emissions and fuel efficiency 
have confirmed that E20 is safe for use under prescribed standards. 
These studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in 
performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. These extensive laboratory studies, field 
validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact 
on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel. 

The Government's assessment is based not only on laboratory research but also on large-scale 
experience after nationwide implementation. India witnesses approximately 8 crore vehicles visiting 
retail outlets every day (around 80% petrol vehicles). 
This is evident from the fact that E15+ blended petrol has been in widespread use for over three-and-
a-half years and E19-E20 fuel for over two-and-a-half years. More than 20 crore two-wheelers and 
over 3 crore petrol cars have been operating on these blends without any verified evidence of 
widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending. Manufacturer 
service data confirm that there is no abnormal corrosion, wear or reduction in vehicle life due to E20 
fuel. Manufacturers continue to honour warranty obligations for vehicles using E20 fuel, providing 
further confidence in its safety and reliability. 
A leading OEM serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025-26, including approximately 1.5 crore 
vehicles that were not originally certified as E20-compatible, and reported no E20-linked corrosion, 
abnormal wear or reduction in component life. A leading 2-wheeler company has reported similar 
field experience. One OEM recently stated that data from 1.4 crore E20-operated vehicles tracked 
over an extended period showed no evidence of ethanol-induced corrosion. ARAI reaffirmed that 
vehicles undergo rigorous international-standard validation before reaching consumers. 
Automobile manufacturers, component suppliers, SIAM, ARAI, testing agencies and Oil Marketing 
Companies were associated with every stage of the scientific evaluation and phased rollout of E20. 
E20 was rolled out only after successful validation of fuel systems, engine durability, drivability, 
reasonable material compatibility and emissions performance. These studies also established that 
legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in performance or abnormal wear and tear 
due to E20.  
At the same time, E20 provides higher octane, better anti-knock performance, improved combustion 
characteristics, smoother acceleration and lower emissions, contributing to cleaner and more 
efficient engine operations emissions, fuel systems and material compatibility have confirmed that 
E20 fuel does not cause abnormal wear and tear or compatibility issues. 
 
Public Sector OMCs procure ethanol from distilleries across the country under the EBP Programme. 
The procurement framework is designed to ensure adequate ethanol availability, provide 
remunerative prices to producers and support the agriculture sector; it is not intended to maximise 
OMC profits.

The retail selling price of E20 petrol is market-determined, and Public Sector OMCs determine 
petrol prices after considering international crude oil prices, exchange rates, freight, taxes, ethanol 
procurement costs and other operational expenses. (For e.g.-the average depot price of petrol during 
March–June 2026 was about Rs.85.8 per litre. Since the retail selling price remained below the 
market-determined level, Public Sector OMCs incurred an average under-recovery of about Rs.11 
per litre on petrol, amounting to approximately Rs 21,300 crore during this period. 
India is the world's third-largest importer of crude oil, meeting nearly 85 per cent of its crude oil 
requirement through imports. During the recent West Asian crisis (starting from 28th February 2026 
and still ongoing), the closure of the Strait simultaneously posed two major challenges such as 
security of supply and escalation in global prices. 
During the recent West Asian crisis, despite sharp increases in global crude prices, India was able to 
shield consumers through calibrated Government interventions, diversified sourcing and the 
increasing contribution of domestically produced biofuels.Since February 2026,even though global 
crude prices rose by around 70–80%, domestic fuel prices increased only by about 7–8%.  
During the peak of West Asia crisis when Indian crude basket touched nearly $135 per barrel, the 
market price of petrol could have been around Rs.125 per litre, however Indian consumers continued 
to pay only Rs.94.77 per litre(ex Delhi) also because OMCs could procure ethanol at ~Rs.70/litre. 
By replacing a part of imported petrol with domestically produced ethanol, India has reduced its 
exposure to international crude oil price volatility and exchange-rate fluctuations. 
This demonstrates that ethanol blending is a strategic investment in energy security, price stability, 
farmer welfare and foreign exchange savings, rather than a revenue-generating exercise for OMCs.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 2042 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
FLIGHTS FROM HISAR AIRPORT 
2042.    SHRI JAI PARKASH                     
     
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government proposes to operate new flights under the UDAN 
Scheme to expand air connectivity from Hisar Airport/Aerodrome in Haryana to 
major cities in the country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of the flights cur rently operating and proposed from Hisar Airport 
along with their destinations and operational status; 
(c) the amount of the funds sanctioned and utilised so far under the UDAN Scheme 
for the development of Hisar Airport including expansion of passenger fa cilities, 
runway, terminal building and other essential infrastructure; and 
(d) whether the Government has prepared any special action plan to develop Hisar 
as a regional aviation hub and attract new airlines and if so, the details thereof and 
the likely timeline fixed in this regard? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d): The Government has launched the next phase of the UDAN Scheme on 
04.07.2026 to further enhance regional air connectivity across the country, connect 
120 new destinations, and serve 4 crore passengers over the next 10 years. As per 
the provisions of the Scheme, Hisar airport is eligible for bidding under the 
underserved Airport category in the forthcoming bidding rounds. Further, t he 
Government of Haryana may identify and propose State Priority Routes for 
inclusion in the bidding process, based on regional connectivity requirements, 
passenger demand and operational feasibility. 
 

At present, Hisar Airport is connected to Ayodhya, Delh i, Chandigarh and Jaipur 
with 14 flights per week by M/s Alliance Air. 
 
With the repeal of the Air Corporations Act in March 1994, the Indian domestic 
aviation has been deregulated. Airlines are free to induct capacity with any aircraft 
type, free to select  whatever markets and network they wish to service depending 
on their operational & commercial viability. 
 
Hisar airport, owned by State Government of Haryana, was identified during 2nd 
round of bidding under the UDAN scheme.  An expenditure of Rs.29.21 cro re was 
incurred for its development and the airport was initially licensed under the 2B 
category. Thereafter, the State Government of Haryana has further upgraded the 
airport at its own cost. The airport has now been licensed as a 4C category.

MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI

DECLINING GROUNDWATER LEVELS 
2044.  Shri ZIA UR REHMAN: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any assess ment of the declining 
groundwater levels in various districts of the coun try and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(b) whether any district-specific groundwater recha rge plans have been 
prepared and if so, the details thereof, State-wise? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a)  Yes,   Dynamic Ground Water Resources of the c ountry are assessed 
annually by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) i n collaboration with the 
State Governments. As per the Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessment, 
2025, the total Annual Ground Water Recharge has be en assessed at 448.52 
Billion Cubic Metres (BCM), the Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource at 
407.75 BCM and the total Annual Ground Water Extrac tion at 247.22 BCM. The 
Stage of Ground Water Extraction for the country ha s been assessed at 60.63 
per cent.  
Out of 6,762 assessment units (Blocks/Taluks/Mandal s), 730 (10.80%) 
have been categorised as Over-exploited, 201 (2.97% ) as Critical, 758 (11.21%) 
as Semi-Critical, 4,946 (73.14%) as Safe and 127 (1 .88%) as Saline. The 

2 
 
State/UT-wise details of groundwater resources are available at the following 
link: https://www.jalshakti-
dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/11/711d8d476bbf498cd90f8038e7371227.pdf 
  
(b) Water being a State subject, sustainable develo pment and management of 
groundwater resources is primarily the responsibili ty of the State Governments 
across all districts of the state. However, the Cen tral Government facilitates 
the efforts of the State Governments by way of tech nical and financial 
assistance through its various schemes and projects . The major steps taken in 
this direction, including the district-level initiatives are provided below: 
i. CGWB successfully completed NAQUIM 1.0 covering cou ntry's 
mappable area of about 25 lakh sq. km and provided a macro-level 
understanding of our nation's groundwater resources . District level 
reports with management plans have been prepared an d shared with 
the state governments. CGWB has embarked upon NAQUI M 2.0, 
focusing on water stressed districts and quality af fected pockets. 
Under NAQUIM 2.0 state-of-the-art technologies are harnessed for 
generating highly detailed scientific data which se rve as an important 
tool for making informed decisions for sustainable groundwater 
management. 
ii. Efforts of the Government for augmenting the groundwater resources of 
the country are mainly channeled through the flagsh ip campaign of Jal 
Shakti Abhiyan (JSA), an annual mission mode programme for taking up 
water harvesting and artificial recharge activities . As per the available 
information, under JSA more than 2 cr water conserv ation and artificial 
recharge works have been taken up through convergen ce in the 
country so far, which has played a key role in enha ncing the 
sustainability of ground water resources in water-stressed districts. 

3 
 
iii. To further strengthen the momentum of JSA, Jal Sanc hay Jan 
Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative has been launched by th e Hon’ble Prime 
Minister in 2024 with a vision to make rain water h arvesting a mass 
movement in the country. By promoting community own ership and 
responsibility, the initiative seeks to develop cos t-eﬀective, local 
solutions tailored to speciﬁc water challenges acro ss districts. More 
than 1.55 crore artificial groundwater recharge and storage works have 
been constructed across the country under this init iative. 
Subsequently, on 01 June 2026 JSJB-Catch the Rain ( CTR) has been 
launched nation-wide for water conservation and artificial recharge. 
iv. M/o Jal Shakti has successfully demonstrated the ef ficacy of 
community led participatory ground water management  through Atal 
Bhujal Yojana, which was implemented in 8,203 water  stressed Gram 
Panchayats across 80 districts in 7 States. Constru ction of various rain 
water harvesting and recharge structures like check  dams, ponds, 
shafts etc. as well as promotion of micro irrigatio n was taken up 
through convergence and by use of incentive funds under the scheme. 
v. Mission Amrit Sarovar was launched by the Governmen t of India 
which aimed at developing and rejuvenating at least  75 water bodies in 
each district of the country. As an outcome nearly 69,000 Amrit 
Sarovars have been constructed/rejuvenated in the c ountry leading to 
enhanced water storage and ground water recharge. 
vi. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs is implem enting the Atal 
Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation ( AMRUT) 2.0 in all 
Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) across the country with a  focus on water 
security, including rejuvenation of water bodies an d development of 
green spaces, which contribute to groundwater recha rge. Under 

4 
 
AMRUT/AMRUT 2.0, States/UTs have taken up 2,960 wat er body 
rejuvenation projects covering about 1.21 lakh acre s and 4,171 parks 
and green space projects covering about 18,168 acre s of permeable 
green area. Further, the Shallow Aquifer Management  (SAM) initiative 
has been launched for scientific management of shal low urban 
aquifers. 
vii. The Department of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare (D A&FW) has been 
implementing the Per Drop More Crop component since  2015-16 to 
improve on-farm water-use efficiency through micro- irrigation. The 
scheme supports efficient irrigation practices in d istricts across the 
country, thereby reducing groundwater extraction an d promoting 
sustainable use of groundwater resources. 
viii. The Government of India launched the Pradhan Mantri  Krishi Sinchayee 
Yojana (PMKSY) in 2015-16 to improve physical acces s to irrigation, 
enhance on-farm water-use efficiency and promote su stainable water 
conservation practices. Under the Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP) component 
of PMKSY, the Repair, Renovation and Restoration (R RR) of Water 
Bodies scheme is being implemented to restore and rejuvenate existing 
water bodies, thereby enhancing water availability and promoting 
groundwater recharge. 
ix. Under VBG-RAMG works relating to water conservation  and water 
harvesting are being carried out.  In Critical and Overexploited Distt. 65 
percent of allocated funds are earmarked for water conservation 
works.

competitiveness and address the grievances  of powerloom and other MSME units in Bhiwandi and 
if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDMUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) & (b): Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), including powerloom units , face 
various operational and business challenges such as access to timely and adequate credit, 
technological obsolescence, fluctuations in input costs, market access and compliance requirements  
in various parts of the country including Bhiwandi in Thane District of Maharashtra.  
 
The Government continuously interacts with industry associations and stakeholders to 
identify constraints faced by MSMEs and takes appropriate policy measures from time to time. 
Further, Government has adopted a comprehensive approach to improve access to finance, 
technology, markets, skilling and ease of doing business for MSMEs across the country, including 
those located in Maharashtra. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

: 2 : 
 
 
 
(c) and (d):  The Ministry of MSME implements various schemes and programmes for 
supporting MSMEs in access to finance, technology, markets, skilling etc. across the country, 
including those in Bhiwandi, Maharashtra. These include:  Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and 
Small Enterprises (CGS)  provides collateral-free credit guarantee coverage for loans extended by 
Member Lending Institutions; Self Reliant Fund (SRI) infuses equity funding in MSMEs having the 
potential and viability to grow and become large units;   Raising and Accelerating MSME 
Performance (RAMP) supports States in strengthening MSME ecosystem, improving market 
access, technology adoption, institutional capacity and implementation of reforms; Procurement and 
Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme facilitates participation of MSMEs in domestic and international 
exhibitions, buyer -seller meets and vendor development programmes ; Entrepreneurship and Skill 
Development Programmes (ESDP) provid es entrepreneurship, skill development and capacity -
building training; and MSME Technology Centres provide advanced technical training, consultancy 
and common facility support. Details of progress under these programs in the state of Maharashtra , 
including Bhiwandi is given at Annexure-I.  
 
 
 Further, the Ministry of Textiles has implemented various schemes from time to time for the 
development of the textile sector, and support has been extended to weavers and entrepreneurs 
under various Central Government schemes implemented on a PAN -India basis, including in the 
Bhiwandi cluste r. These schemes are operational only for roll over liabilities. Details of support 
extended to Bhiwandi under these schemes is given at Annexure-II.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2046 
TO BE ANSWERED ON JULY 30, 2026 
 
FUND ALLOCATION FOR ANDHRA PRADESH UNDER PMAY-U 
 
NO. 2046 SHRI SRIBHARAT MATHUKUMILLI:    
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of Central Assistance sanctioned, released and utilised  
under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY -U) along with the 
number of houses sanctioned, grounded and completed, State/UT -wise 
including Andhra Pradesh, particularly for Visakhapatnam district;  
(b) the reasons for Andhra Pradesh’s completion rate remaining 
significantly lower than several other States despite having one of the 
highest numbers of houses sanctioned in the country;  
(c) whether this gap is attributable to shortage of Central funds released, 
delays in State-level fund utilisation, land-related issues, contractor non-
performance or technical/planning capacity constraints and if so, the 
details thereof, State/UT -wise, particularly district -wise for Andhra 
Pradesh;  
(d) the time-bound action plan, if any, to expedite completion of pending 
houses across Andhra Pradesh, particularly in Visakhapatnam; and  
(e) whether any additional financial or technical assistance is proposed 
and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
(a)  to (e): Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been 
implementing Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY -U) since 
25.06.2015 to provide all weather pucca houses with basic civic 
amenities to eligible urban beneficiaries across the country. Based on 
the learnings from the experiences of implementation of PMAY -U, 
MoHUA has revamped the scheme and launched PMAY-U 2.0 ‘Housing  
 
...2/- 
 
 

-2- 
for All’ Mission with effect from 01.09.2024 for implementation in urban 
areas across the country to support 1 crore additional eligible 
beneficiaries. The Scheme Guidelines may be accessed at https://pmay-
urban.gov.in/uploads/guidelines/Operational-Guidelines-of-PMAY-U-
2.pdf. 
 
Based on the project proposal submitted by States/UTs, a total of 127.68 
lakh houses under PMAY -U and PMAY -U 2.0 have been sanctioned by 
the Ministry. Out of which, 121.03 lakh houses have been grounded and 
99.07 lakh are completed/ delivered to the benefi ciaries across the 
country as on 13.07.2026. Under PMAY-U 2.0 a total of 16.20 lakh houses 
have been sanctioned across the country with the Central Assistance 
of ₹23,383 crores.  
PMAY-U has been extended up to 30.09.2026 only for the completion of 
houses sanctioned on or before 31.03.2024 and started on or before 
31.12.2025. Based on the project proposals submitted by State of 
Andhra Pradesh, a total of 19.07 lakh houses have been sanctioned 
under PMAY-U, of which 3.71 are non-starter houses. Against the 15.36 
lakh started houses, a total of 11.38 lakh houses have been completed 
and 10.75 lakh houses are occupied, so far.  
Under PMAY-U, the State is eligible for a maximum Central Assistance 
of ₹23,507.44 crore for started houses. However, Central Assistance 
amounting to ₹23,665.79 crore has already been released to the State, 
resulting in an excess release of ₹158.35 crore. Accordingly, the 
Government of Andhra Pradesh has been requested to refund the excess 
amount released by the Ministry. Furthermore, any excess amount 
available with State Government is adjusted against further releases 
under PMAY-U/PMAY-U 2.0.  
Under PMAY-U 2.0, a total of 61,084 houses have been sanctioned in the 
State of Andhra Pradesh, out of which 43,947 houses have been 
grounded. Of these, 1,980 houses have been completed/delivered to the 
beneficiaries. Further, Central Assistance amounting to ₹882.32 crore 
has been sanctioned, of which ₹406.39 crore has been released to the 
State. 
...3/- 
 
 

-3- 
A total of 1,87,595 houses have been sanctioned for the district of 
Vishakhapatnam, of which 49,270 are non- starter. Out of 1,36,908 
started houses, 1,09,094 have been completed. The committed Central 
Assistance is ₹2,930 crore of which, ₹2,289 crore has already  been 
released. The details of houses sanctioned, grounded and completed 
along with Central Assistance approved, released and utilized under the 
schemes across the country including Andhra Pradesh are at Annexure. 
The progress of the scheme can also be accessed on the PMAY -U 
dashboard (https://dashboard.pmay-urban.gov.in). 
The timeline for completion of houses/projects varies from State to 
State and it generally takes 12- 36 months in different verticals of the 
scheme and as per Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) of respective 
projects.  
The completion timeline for houses depends on various factors like 
availability of encumbrance free land, financial constraints of States 
and beneficiaries, issues related to trunk infrastructure, increase in the 
cost of construction materials, delays in obtaining statutory 
clearances/No Objection Certificates (NOCs) and disruptions caused by 
unforeseen circum stances including State of Andhra Pradesh and 
Vishakhapatnam. The Ministry conducts regular reviews with the 
States/UTs to monitor progress of implementation of the scheme and 
expedite completion & occupancy of sanctioned houses within the 
stipulated timeline.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 2047 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
GREENFIELD AIRPORT PROJECT IN DAHOD  
2047.    SHRI JASWANTSINH SUMANBHAI BHABHOR      
  
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the present status of the Greenfield Airport project in Dahod district of 
Gujarat as on date; 
(b) the expected timeline fixed for commencement of construction and the 
projected date for operationalisation of the said airport; and 
(c) the total expenditure sanctioned by the Government for the said project 
under the Greenfield Airports Policy? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) & (b): Government of India (GoI) has formulated a G reenfield Airports 
(GFA) Policy, 2008. As per the policy, if any airport developer including State 
Government desires to develop an airport, they are required to identify a 
suitable site and get the Pre -feasibility Study conducted and submit a proposal 
to GoI for 'Site Clearance' followed by 'In-Principle' approval. 
 
GoI has not received any proposal seeking 'Site Clearance' under the GFA 
Policy for development of a Greenfield airport in Dahod. Further, the timeline 
for completion of the airport projects de pend upon several factors such as land 
acquisition, availability of mandatory clearances including environmental 
clearances, financial closure etc. 
 
(c): As per the GFA Policy, the responsibility of the implementation of airport 
project including its funding rests with the Project Proponent.
