(a) whether the Government has reviewed the recent analysis 
indicating that the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) has fell short of 
meeting several of its originally envisaged technology -driven and 
integrated urban development objectives; 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the proportion of incomplete 
Smart City projects in the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar 
Haveli and Daman and Diu from the last year to date along with 
the details of the Central funds released, utilised and remaining 
unutilised for these projects; 
(c) the assessment of the Government regarding operational 
challenges of Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs), particularly 
concerning governance gaps, personnel management 
uncertainties and the decline in functional capacity after the 
formal expiry of the Mission’s tenure; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to review and redesign the 
framework of the SCM and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) and (b): The Smart Cities Mission (SCM) was launched on 25
th  
June 2015 to develop 100 cities through an area- based approach—
retrofitting, redevelopment, greenfield projects, and pan- city smart 
solutions and covered sectors like smart mobility, Water, Sanitation, 
Hygiene (WASH), smart governance, smart energy, environment etc., 
with each project having defined timelines. The cities under the Smart 
Cities Mission have been developed based on Smart City Proposals 
(SCPs) received from States/UTs across various sectors duly approved  
…2/- 

-2- 
by State High Powered Steering Committee (HPSC), chaired by the 
Chief Secretary. 
 
Under SCM, 8,064 projects worth ₹1,64,811 Cr were taken up since 
inception of the Mission. As on 31.03.2026, 7,790 projects (97%) worth 
₹1,56,257 Cr have been completed. As reported by States/ UTs as on 
31.03.2026, the Central Government’s ₹48,000 Cr allocation achieved 
99% fund claims (₹47,458 Cr) and 98% utilization (₹46,377 Cr) by 
States/UTs.  
 
The State/UT-wise and city-wise details of projects including Dadra and 
Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu along with central financial 
assistance claimed and utilised under SCM are enclosed as Annexure. 
 
(c): Post closure of SCM on 31.03.2025, Ministry of Housing and Urban 
Affairs (MoHUA) has issued Advisory No. 27 dated 10
th June, 2025 to all 
States/ UTs. As per the advisory, the Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) 
are to ensure the timely completion of all ongoing SCM projects and 
prepare O&M plans for the assets created. The Advisory has further 
outlined the envisioned future role of SPVs of smart cities and a 
roadmap for the continued functioning of ICCCs.  The advisory 
underscores repurposing of SPVs to meet emerging urban challenges. 
 
(d): No. Does not arise.

TO BE ANSWERED ON- 30/07/2026 
 
IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGES ON CHANGPA TRIBAL COMMUNITY IN 
LADAKH 
2049.   SHRI MOHMAD HANEEFA: 
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of climate change, shrinking grazing 
pastures, changing snowfall patterns and declining livestock productivity on the livelihood 
and traditional nomadic lifestyle of the Changpa tribal community in Ladakh and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b) the details of welfare and livelihood schemes being implemented for Changpa families 
during the last five years; 
(c) whether any special programme has been launched for pasture development, veterinary 
healthcare, mobile service delivery, education, housing and income enhancement of Changpa 
pastoralists and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the details of funds released under various schemes of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for 
the Changthang region during the last five years; and 
(e) the measures being taken to strengthen the long-term socio-economic resilience and 
preserve the traditional culture and livelihood of the Changpa community? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
(a): The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has not undertaken any study to assess the impact of climate 
change, shrinking grazing pastures, changing snowfall patterns and declining livestock 
productivity on the livelihood and traditional nomadic lifestyle of the Changpa tribal 
community in Ladakh. 

(b): Changpa families, being members of a Scheduled Tribe, are eligible beneficiaries under 
the welfare and livelihood schemes implemented by this Ministry and other line 
Ministries/Departments during the last five years, including: 
(i) Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN); 
(ii) Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA); 
(iii) Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS); 
(iv) Pre-Matric, Post-Matric and National Overseas Scholarships for Scheduled Tribe 
students; 
(v) Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM); 
(c): Yes. Under the umbrella of DAJGUA, targeted interventions have been taken up for 
remote tribal habitations including Mobile Medical Units; mobile network delivery; 
residential hostel facilities; pucca housing under PM-AWAS (Gramin) etc. Additionally, 
livelihood and income-enhancement support for Pashmina wool production, marketing 
linkages and value addition is being undertaken through TRIFED. 
(d): Under PMJVM scheme, TRIFED has released an amount of ₹15 lakhs for establishment 
of the VDVK, Durbuk. The details of funds sanctioned and released for EMRSs to the UT of 
Ladakh in last 5 years is as follows: 
Financial Year Rs. in lakhs 
2021-22 10.00 
2022-23 450.00 
2023-24 800.00 
2024-25 17.41 
2025-26 400.00 
  
(e): To strengthen long-term socio-economic resilience and preserve the traditional culture 
and livelihood of the Changpa community, the following measures, among others, are being 
taken: 
 Saturation of basic infrastructure and services in Changthang habitations under PM-
JANMAN/DAJGUA;  
 During the last five years, TRIFED has procured Pashmina products (Shawls and 
Stoles) worth ₹18,847,291 from Ladakh-based artisans. Since the raw Pashmina used 

in these products is sourced from the Changpa community, these procurements have 
indirectly contributed to the livelihood and economic well-being of the Changpa 
pastoralists.  
 Further, an empanelment camp is proposed to be organised in the Changthang region in 
August’2026 with the objective of identifying and empanelling eligible artisans from 
the Changpa Tribal Community. This initiative is expected to facilitate their direct 
participation in marketing and procurement programmes, thereby strengthening their 
livelihood opportunities. 
 Documentation and promotion of Changpa culture, language and traditional knowledge 
through tribal research institute.

DEVELOPMENT OF AIRPORT IN WEST BENGAL

Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has any proposal to set up new airport in West 
Bengal; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof, location-wise? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) & (b): Gov ernment of India (GoI) has formulated a Greenfield Airports 
(GFA) Policy, 2008 for development of Greenfield airports in the country. As

2051. SHRI DARSHAN SINGH CHOUDHARY: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is implementing any comprehensive action plan under the Micro 
and Small Enterprises - Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP) to promote competitiveness, 
productivity and employment generation among industries in the country and if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b)  the details of clusters sanctioned, projects completed, funds allocated and utilised and the 
enterprises benefited under the Programme during the last three years, State-wise; 
 
(c)  whether the Government proposes to provide additional financial and technical assistance 
for the establishment of new Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) clusters relating to 
agriculture-based industries, handicrafts, handlooms, food processing, engineering, forest produce 
and other local industries and also for Common Facility Centres (CFCs), testing laboratories,

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER

ALLOCATION OF POWER FROM CENTRAL POWER PROJECTS TO  
UTTAR PRADESH 
 
†2052. SHRI ARUN KUMAR SAGAR: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Union Government has taken any steps to ensure the allocation 
of power from central power projects to the State of Uttar Pradesh in 
accordance with its requirements and to ensure uninterrupted power supply in 
the Scheduled Caste dominated Shahjahanpur Parliamentary Constituency; and  
 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) & (b):  The Government of India has allocated 11,520.53 MW of power to 
Uttar Pradesh from Central Sector Generating Station (CGS), as on 30.06.2026, 
which comprises 11,269.93 MW of firm power and 250.6 MW power from 
unallocated quota. 
 
Electricity being a concurrent subject, the supp ly and distribution of 
electricity to the various categories of consumers/areas/districts in a State/UT 
is looked after by the respective Power Utility/State Government. Further, The 
Central Government supplements the efforts of the State Governments by 
establishing power plants through Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs) 
and allocate power from them to the various States / UTs. 
 
To ensure generation capacity remains ahead of projected demand, all 
the States, in consultation with CEA, have prepared their “Resource Adequacy 
Plans (RAPs)”, which are dynamic 10 -year rolling plans and includes power 
generation as well as power procurement planning. 
 
The details of Power Supply Position for the State of Uttar Pradesh in 
terms of Energy for the last three f inancial years and current year (upto June, 
2026) is given at Annexure. The ‘energy supplied’ has been commensurate 
with the ‘energy requirement’ with only a marginal gap which is generally on 
account of constraints in the State transmission / distribution network. 
………2. 
 

- 2 - 
 
Following steps have been taken to support States/Distribution Utilities 
to provide uninterrupted power supply in the States/UTs including the State of 
Uttar Pradesh: 
 
(i) Government of India launched “Revamped Distribution Sector Schem e 
(RDSS) in July, 2021 with the objective of improving the quality of power 
supply through a financially sustainable and operationally efficient 
distribution sector. The scheme has a total outlay of Rs.3,03,758 crore, 
including Gross Budgetary Support fro m the Central Government of 
Rs.97,631 crore. The sunset date of the scheme is 31.03.2028. Under the 
scheme, financial assistance is being provided to the Distribution 
Utilities for loss reduction infrastructure works and smart metering 
works. Loss reduction  works include replacement of old conductors, 
creation of new substations, upgradation of Substations, installation of 
new Distribution Transformers (DTs), upgradation of DTs, feeder 
segregation works etc. Under the scheme, loss reduction infrastructure 
works amounting to        Rs.21,782 crore and smart metering work s 
amounting to Rs. 18,956 crore have been sanctioned for the State of 
Uttar Pradesh. In Shahjahanpur Parliamentary Constituency, loss 
reduction infrastructure works amounting to Rs.230.88 crore and smart 
metering works amounting to Rs. 234.02 crore have been sanctioned. 
The loss reduction works have achieved physical progress of around 
61%. 
 
(ii) Government of India has supplemented the efforts of the States through 
schemes namely Deen Dayal Upadh yaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) 
and Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) for 
strengthening of the rural distribution network and electrification of 
villages and households. As reported by the States, all the inhabited un -
electrified censu s villages in the country were electrified. A total of 
18,374 villages were electrified during DDUGJY, including 1,498 villages 
in the State of Uttar Pradesh. Under DDUGJY and thereafter during 
SAUBHAGYA, electrification of all willing households was compl eted. A 
total of 2.86 crore households were electrified during the SAUBHAGYA 
period, including 91.8 lakh households in the State of Uttar Pradesh and 
1,23,284 households in Shahjahanpur Lok Sabha Constituency. Both the 
schemes stand closed as on 31.03.2022 . Government of India is further 
supporting States for grid electrification of left-out households, including 
households belonging to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) 
under PM-JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan), 
tribal households under DA -JGUA (Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh 
Abhiyan), Scheduled Caste households under Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit 
Jaati Abhyuday Yojna (PM-AJAY) and remote & border households under 
Vibrant Village Program (VVP), under RDSS. Till date, under RDSS, works 
have been sanctioned for electrification of 13.65 lakh households 
including 2,58,700 households in the State of Uttar Pradesh and 2,924 
households in Shahjahanpur Lok Sabha Constituency.  
……..3. 

 
 
- 3 - 
 
 
(iii) As per rule 10 of the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020, the 
distribution licensee shall supply 24x7 power to all consumers. However, 
the State Commission may specify lower hours of supply for some 
categories of consumers.

FLOOD MANAGEMENT IN MEERUT 
†2054.  Shri ARUN GOVIL: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the details and total number of barrages situat ed on the Ganga River 
between Haridwar and Bijnor; 
(b) whether the Government is aware that several vi llages in Meerut district 
are affected by floods due to the release of excess  water from the Bijnor 
Barrage during the monsoon and if so, the details t hereof along with the steps 
taken by the Government for a permanent solution to the flood problem; 
(c) whether the Government has conducted any study regarding the possibility 
of an alternative water drainage project or constru ction of a canal for safe 
discharge of excess water from the Bijnor Barrage a nd to provide a permanent 
solution of the problem of flooding in Meerut distr ict and if so, the details and 
findings thereof; and 
(d) whether such study has examined the possibility  of diverting excess water 
to the Kali River or any other suitable watercourse  and if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 

2 
 
(a)  There are two barrages on the Ganga River betw een Haridwar and Bijnor, 
namely, Bhimgoda barrage in Haridwar district and C haudhary Charan Singh 
Madhya Ganga Barrage in Bijnor district for irrigation purpose. 
(b)  Flood management and anti-erosion schemes are formulated and 
implemented by the concerned State Governments as p er their respective 
priorities. The Union Government supplements the ef forts of the States by 
providing technical guidance and promotional financ ial assistance for flood 
management in critical areas. 
The Government of Uttar Pradesh has informed that t he total length of the 
Ganga River in Meerut district is approximately 48. 00 km. To mitigate the 
adverse impact of floods during the monsoon season,  the 10.80 km long 
Hastinapur Embankment has been constructed in Meeru t district as a 
continuation of the previously constructed Ramraj E mbankment in 
Muzaffarnagar district. The embankment provides flo od protection to a 
population of 7,915 and safeguards approximately 6, 936.20 hectares of 
agricultural land spread across 15 villages situate d along the right bank of the 
river, namely, Fatehpur Prem, Haripur, Dabkhedi, Sh erpur, Shirjepur, 
Rustampur alias Bhikund, Hadipur Gaonri, Parsapur H ansapur, Bhagupur, 
Manpur, Rathoda Kalan, Latifpur, Chamraud, Kunhaida , Rupda, Lalpur, and 
Manoharpur. 
Further, two flood management projects on the Ganga  River in the Meerut 
and Bijnor districts of Uttar Pradesh, having a tot al cost of Rs. 41.41 
crore, have been completed with central assistance amounting to Rs. 20.97 
crore released under the Flood Management and Borde r Areas Programme 
(FMBAP) Scheme of Union Government. 
(c) & (d)   The Government of Uttar Pradesh has inf ormed that no such study 
has been undertaken.

IMPACT OF PROPOSED MEKEDATU DAM ON TAMIL NADU 
2055.  THIRU DAYANIDHI MARAN: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Union Government has assessed the l ikely impact of the State 
Government of Karnataka’s proposed Mekedatu Dam on irrigation, agricultural 
productivity and the livelihood of Cauvery delta fa rmers in Tamil Nadu and if so, 
the findings thereof; 
(b) whether the Union Government has received repre sentations from the State 
Government of Tamil Nadu and farmers' organisations  opposing the project and if 
so, the details thereof along with the action taken thereon; 
(c) whether the Union Government has examined the p roposed project's effect on 
the timely release of Cauvery water for cultivation  in Tamil Nadu and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(d) whether any consultation has been held with the  State Government of Tamil 
Nadu before processing approvals for the project and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Union Government to prot ect the interests of Cauvery 
delta farmers and ensure that no project adversely affecting Tamil Nadu's rightful 
share of river water is approved in violation of existing Tribunal and Supreme Court 
directions? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 

2 
 
(a) Detailed Project Report (DPR) of Mekedatu Balan cing Reservoir cum Drinking 
Water Project, Karnataka submitted in 2019 has been  returned to the project 
authority with the request to submit the revised DP R in compliance with CWDT 
award and as per the extant CWC guidelines.  
(b) to (d)  The Government of India has taken note of the representations received 
from the Government of Tamil Nadu and farmers' orga nisations expressing 
concerns regarding the possible impacts of the prop osed project on the Cauvery 
Delta region, including drinking water availability  in other 
districts. Representations received in respect of  any project are examined, as 
appropriate, during appraisal of the project in acc ordance with the applicable 
procedure.  
  As per the Hon’ble Supreme Court judgment dated 1 6.02.2018 regarding the 
Cauvery water dispute, there is no mention that Sta te of Karnataka has to obtain 
the consent of the other riparian States namely Tam il Nadu, Kerala and UT of 
Puducherry to construct any kind of structure acros s river Cauvery. Hon’ble 
Supreme Court in its Order dated 16.02.2018 has fou nd the Clause XVIII of Cauvery 
Water Dispute Tribunal (CWDT) Award of 2007 appropr iate and reiterated in its 
Order that “Nothing in the order of this Tribunal s hall impair the right or power or 
authority of any State to regulate within its bound aries the use of water or to enjoy 
the benefit of waters within that State in a manner  not inconsistent with the order 
of this Tribunal”.  
(e)  In exercise of the powers conferred by section  6A of Inter-State River Water 
Disputes (ISRWD) Act, 1956, the Central Government vide  Gazette notification 
dated 01.06.2018 notified the Cauvery Water Managem ent Scheme (CWMS), inter-
alia , constituting the Cauvery Water Management Authori ty (CWMA) and Cauvery 
Water Regulation Committee (CWRC), to give effect t o the decision of the Cauvery 
Water Disputes Tribunal, as modified by the Hon’ble  Supreme Court vide  its Order 
dated 16.02.2018.

ANSWERED ON 30/07/2026 
  
EFFECTIVENESS OF CLEANLINESS AND SANITATION INITIATIVES 
  
2056. SMT. MALVIKA DEVI: 
  
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any benchmark or performance indicators have been prescribed to evaluate the 
effectiveness of cleanliness and sanitation initiatives in rural areas and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the measures being taken by the Government to ensure that rural areas are accorded priority 
under the Swachh Bharat Mission - Gramin (SBM-G); and 
(c) the steps being taken by the Government to achieve hundred per cent sanitation coverage 
in rural areas, particularly in aspirationa l districts along with the details of the financial 
assistance, monitoring mechanisms and awareness programmes being implemented to achieve 
this objective? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
  
(a) & (b) Sanitation is State subject. Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II [SBM(G) -
Phase II], is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, implemented by States and Union Territory (UTs) 
Governments in rural areas within their respective jurisdictions. SBM(G) -Phase II is being 
implemented in rural areas of the country during the period from 2020 -21 to 2026 -27, with 
focus on Open Defecation Free (ODF) sustainability and to cover all the villages with solid and 
liquid waste management (SLWM) arrangements with visual clea nliness i.e. converting 
villages from ODF to ODF Plus (Model). The benchmarks for declaration of villages as Open 
Defecation Free (ODF) Plus under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase -II and the 
categorization are as follows: 
• ODF Plus Aspiring: A village which is sustaining its ODF status and has arrangements 
for Solid Waste Management OR Liquid Waste Management; 
• ODF Plus Rising: A village which is sustaining its ODF status and has arrangements for 
both Solid Waste Management and Liquid Waste Management: 

Page 2 of 4 
 
• ODF Plus Model: A village which is sustaining its ODF status and has arrangements for 
both Solid Waste Management and Liquid Waste Management; observes visual 
cleanliness, i.e., minimal litter, minimal stagnant wastewater, no plastic waste dump in 
public places; and displays ODF Plus Information, Education & Communication (IEC) 
messages. 
(c) Government of India had launched Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) [SBM(G)], a 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme, with effect from 2 nd October, 2014 with the aim to attain Open 
Defecation Free (ODF) India by 2 nd October, 2019 by providing access to toilet facilities in 
rural areas. More than 10 crore individual household latrines (IHHLs) were constructed under 
the programme between 2014 to 2019, as per the data reported by the States/UTs.  As a result, 
sanitation coverage in the rural areas of the country has increased from 39% as on 02.10.2014 
to 100% and all  villages declared themselves ODF in 2019. SBM(G) -Phase-II is a Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme, implemented  by States/UTs Governments in rural areas with focus on 
Open Defecation Free (ODF) sustainability and to cover all the villages with solid and liquid 
waste management arrangements with visual cleanliness i.e. converting the villages from ODF 
to ODF Plus (Model). 
Government of India has been providing financial and technical support to the State/UT 
Governments to supplement their efforts to improve overall sanitation and SLWM in the rural 
areas. Besides budgetary support from DDWS (Centre Share) and State share, the States /UTs 
also converge funds through Finance Commission grants and various Central/State schemes, 
as per the guidelines, as applicable. Further, under SBM(G) Phase II funds are not released 
component-wise or project -wise or separately for Aspirational District s by this Department. 
However, States/UTs can plan for providing sanitation and hygiene facilities as per the local 
demand in rural areas, including villages in Aspirational Districts, under their overall AIP. 
Apart from providing budgetary support, Depart ment of Drinking Water and Sanitation 
(DDWS) issues operational guidelines, advisories and monitors the implementation of the 
programme.  
State/UT-wise Central share of funds released under SBM(G) Phase-II from FY 2020-21 to FY 
2025-26 is placed at Annexure. 
Under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), following digital monitoring portals and mobile 
applications are being used for monitoring the progress of the programme  across 34 
States/UTs: 
(i) SBM-G Portal & Dashboard: A centralized portal  
(https://swachhbharatmission.ddws.gov.in) and dashboard 
(https://sbm.gov.in/sbmgdashboard/statesdashboard.aspx) is used for monitoring progress 
under SBM(G) at the National, State, district, block and village levels. The SBM(G) dashboard 
captures the progress of States/UTs on  various components of SBM(G) including Open 
Defecation Free (ODF) Plus status, construction of Individual Household Latrines (IHHLs) 
and Community Sanitary Complexes (CSCs), solid and liquid waste management (SLWM) 
assets and Information, Education & Communication (IEC). 

Page 3 of 4 
 
(ii) Mobile Applications: The mSBM and SBM2.0 mobile applications have been developed 
under SBM(G) which are used for geo -tagging of IHHLs and geo -tagging of solid and liquid 
waste management assets (including CSCs) respectively. SBM 2.0 m obile application also 
captures assets constructed under the programme. 
SBM(G) Phase II is not just about constructing infrastructure for ODF Plus villages but aims 
at behaviour change of the masses to adopt better sanitation and hygiene practices. 
Accordingly, Information, Education and Communication (IEC) is integral to the programme, 
which lays foundation for sustainable behavioural change and community partnership Jan 
Bhagidari in the programme. It also strengthens community ownership of assets created under 
the programme.  Since sanitation is a State subject, States/UTs are to develop and implement 
IEC campaigns, focusing on various components of the programme including sanitation, 
hygiene and waste management. Under SBM(G) Phase II, for IEC and Capacit y Building 
activities, expenditure up to 5% of the total project funds is permissible with up to 2% to be 
utilized at the Central level and up to 3% at the States/District level.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2058 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
STATUS OF NATIONAL HIGHWAY PROJECTS IN NASHIK  
2058.   SHRI RAJABHAU PARAG PRAKASH WAJE:    
Will the MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a)     the details and present status of all National Highway projects 
sanctioned in Nashik district during the last five years, indicating 
project-wise length, cost, physical progress and target completion dates; 
(b)     the current status of the proposed Nashik Outer Ring Road, 
including DPR, land acquisition, financial approval and reasons for the 
delay in commencement; 
(c)     the details and present status of all Greenfield  Highway projects 
proposed or approved in Nashik district including alignment, land 
acquisition and timelines; 
(d)     whether cost escalation and execution delays have adversely 
affected these projects and if so, the reasons and responsibility fixed; 
(e)     the status of land acquisition and fund release, project-wise; and 
(f)      the time -bound action plan to complete all pending National 
Highway, Outer Ring Road and Greenfield Highway projects before 
further cost escalation and inconvenience to the public? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a)     The status of all National Highways (NHs) projects sanctioned in 
Nashik district during the last five years including current year is 
annexed. 
(b)     The Government in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is 
primarily responsible for development and maintenance of NHs. Nashik 
Outer Ring Road is not a NH and the same is being developed by the 
State Government of Maharashtra through its own funds.

access control Greenfield Expressway project from Nashik -Adgoan-

acquisition have been declared for 90% area and compensation 
disbursed for 25% area. The bids for award of civil construction work are 
invited with Bid Due Date on 20.08.2026. The civil construction works 
are targeted for completion in Financial Year (FY) 2030-31. 
  
(f)      The Government has taken number of steps to ensure timely 
completion of NH projects. These include streamlining and expediting 
land acquisition using “Bhoomirashi” portal and GIS -based Land 
Acquisition Plan, revamping “Parivesh” Portal through Ministry of 
Environment, Forest and Climate Change, to facilitate faster forest and 
environmental clearances, enabling online approval of General 
Arrangement of Drawings (GAD) of Road Over Bridge / Road Under Bridge

and resolution of bottlenecks / hindrances in ongoing projects, in active

clearances with defined timelines for various approvals. 
  
Government has put in place a strong framework using multiple 
mechanisms for monitoring project progress and contractor 
inefficiencies. Regular review meetings are conducted at various levels 
with stakeholders to assess project progress, and critical projects such

appointment.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
 LOK SABHA 
  UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2059 
   ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026   
INCREASE IN HEIGHT OF CULVERTS/BRIDGES 
2059. SHRI JAGADISH SHETTAR: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
 
 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any measures are being contemplated to increase the 
height of culverts/bridges from the present 4.5 metres to 5.5 metres 
while undertaking construction of highways to facilitate easy 
movement of vehicles beneath them; and 
  
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)  
 
(a) to (b) Culverts and bridges are cross -drainage structures on 
National Highways which facilit ate the drainage of natural 
watercourses across the National Highways. The vent size, span 
arrangement and height of such structures are governed by 
hydraulic considerations at the location, namely the design 
discharge, the highest flood level, the permiss ible afflux and scour 
considerations, and not by the requirement of movement of vehicles 
beneath the highway as they are meant for crossing of water 
channel. 

However, movement of traffic across and beneath a National 
Highway is  provided through grade -separated structures, namely 
Vehicular Underpasses (VUP), Light Vehicle Underpasses 
(LVUP)/Small Vehicle Underpasses (SVUP), Cattle Underpasses 
(CUP) and Pedestrian Underpasses (PUP). A minimum vertical 
clearance of 5.5 metres is already prescribed for Vehicula r 
Underpasses (VUP) on National Highways, and is provided while 
undertaking construction, four/six -laning and upgradation of 
National Highways. Structures falling in the LVUP/SVUP/CUP/PUP 
categories (height varying from 3.0 m to 4.5 m) are, by design, 
provided with lower vertical clearances, since they are intended to 
serve restricted categories of traffic including pedestrians.

Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of water supply, sewerage, storm -water drainage, parks 
and urban infrastructure projects sanctioned and developed under 
the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation 
(AMRUT) in Karnataka during each of the last five years, district -
wise, including Chitradurga Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b)  the details of funds sanctioned, released, utilised and expenditure 
incurred under the said mission in Karnataka including Chitradurga 
Lok Sabha Constituency, project-wise; 
(c)  the present status of each project indicating the number of projects 
completed, under implementation and pending along with the 
reasons for delay, if any; and 
(d)  the steps taken by the Government to expedite the completion of 
pending projects, ensure timely release of funds and improve urban 
infrastructure under the said mission in Karnataka, particularly in 
Chitradurga Lok Sabha Constituency? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (d):  Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation 
(AMRUT) launched in the year 2015 in selected 500 cities and towns (now 
485 cities including 15 merged cities)  across the country was focused 
on development of basic infrastructure in the sectors of water supply , 
sewerage and septage management , storm water drainage,  green 
spaces and parks , etc. Under the Mission the States/ Union Territories 
were empowered to select, appraise, prioritise and implement the 
projects as per broad framework of Mission guidelines.  
…2/- 
 

-2- 
Under AMRUT, as updated by the State of Karnataka on AMRUT portal, 
the State has grounded 404 projects worth ₹5112.54 crore of which 
works worth ₹5061.97 crore have been physically completed. The 
approved projects include 44 water supply projects worth ₹2213.09 
crore, 55 sewerage and septage management projects worth ₹2499.92 
crore, 83 storm w ater drainage projects worth ₹238.06 crore and 181 
parks and green space projects worth ₹112.91 crore. The status of the 
projects in the State, City-wise including Chitradurga are available on the 
website  
amrut.mohua.gov.in/approvedProjectsAmrut/ulb/OXhRK3hRdEZJSC9hd
mxYZXVTM0ZFdz09.  All the 15 projects taken up by the State under 
AMRUT in Chitradurga city have been completed.       
  
Funds under AMRUT we re released to the States and not city -wise or 
project-wise. Under AMRUT, total Central assistance of ₹2258.85 crore 
has been released to the State for the projects including those in 
Chitradurga, against which the State has submitted utilisation of 
₹2238.78 crore.  
 
The Mission guidelines has provision of the State High Powered Steering 
Committee (SHPSC) headed by the Chief Secretary of the State to 
monitor and supervise implementation of the scheme at the State/ UT 
level. Further, an Apex Committee constituted under the Mission, 
reviews and m onitor the Mission periodically. Also, the progress is 
periodically reviewed and monitored through regular video conferences/ 
webinars/ workshops/ site- visits etc. by Ministry of Housing and Urban 
Affairs (MoHUA) with the States/ UTs. There is a dedicated AMRUT online 
portal for tracking the progress and project -wise outcomes provided by 
the States/ UTs.  
 
The State has informed that periodic review meetings are conducted by 
the State Government along with Urban Local Bodies ( ULBs), and 
implementing agencies to track project progress, identify bottlenecks, 
and timely completion. Further, regular trainings and capacity building is 
carried out for implementing agencies and ULB Officials. Contractors and 
implementing agencies have been directed to deploy additional 
manpower, machinery, and technical resources to expedite delayed 
works.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2063 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
 
REDUCTION IN TRANSMISSION AND DISTRIBUTION LOSSES 
 
†2063. SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the targets fixed for reducing transmission and distribution losses in the country 
during each of the last three years and the current year and the achievements made 
in this regard, State-wise;  
 
(b) whether the Government proposes to provide performance -linked incentives to 
the States for reducing transmission and distribution losses; and  
 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (c): The transmission losses in the country are around 3-4% on an annual basis. 
Distribution losses in the distribution network, along with the losses on account of 
shortfall in collection of revenue, are together reported as  Aggregate Technical & 
Commercial (AT&C) losses of the distribution utilities.  
 
Government of India (GoI) launched the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme 
(RDSS) in July 2021 with the objective of improving the quality of power through a 
financially sustainable and operationally efficient distribution sector. The scheme 
has an outlay of Rs. 3,03,758 crore and estimated Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) 
from Central Government of Rs. 97,631 crore.  
 
Under the scheme, financial assistance is being provided to th e distribution 
utilities for loss reduction infrastructure and smart metering works. Projects worth 
Rs. 1.53 lakh crore for loss reduction infrastructure and Rs. 1.31 lakh crore for smart 
metering works have been sanctioned under the scheme. Release of funds under the 
scheme is linked with performance of the distribution utilities against operational 
and financial parameters including the AT&C losses. Distribution utility wise AT&C 
loss reduction targets and achievements are enclosed at Annexure. 
 
With concerted efforts of the Central and State Governments and as a result 
of various reform measures undertaken, there has been a reduction in overall 
transmission and distribution losses. AT&C losses across the country have reduced 
from 21.91% in FY21 to 15.04% in FY25. These collective efforts have also resulted 
in distribution utilities, on an aggregate basis, achieving a profit after tax (PAT) of 
Rs 2,701 crore in FY25 for the first time since coming into force of Electricity Act, 
2003.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2064 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
  
PLANTATION OF TREES ALONG NHs 
  
2064. DR. SAMBIT PATRA: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
  
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has formulated any policy for planting 
trees and greening along sides of National Highways (NHs) in the 
country and if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) the details of monitoring and inspection carried out for compliance 
with the targets of plantation and maintenance parameters on NHs; 
  
(c) whether any policy is being implemented by the Government for 
penalising or awarding the contractors for negligent behavior or 
excellent work in plantation on the National Highways (NHs) and if so, 
the details thereof; and 
  
(d) the details of the targets set and achievements made regarding 
plantation of trees on National Highways by National Highways 
Authority of India (NHAI) during the last three years, State/UT-wise? 
  
  
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)  
  

(a)   The Government has formulated the Green Highways 
(Plantation, Transplantation, Beautification and Maintenance) Policy, 
2015 for planting trees and greenery along and on the sides of National 
Highways (NHs). 
The policy deals with avenue and median plantation, landscaping, 
beautification and transplantation wherever feasible, along the NHs. It 
aims at environmental conservation, carbon sequestration, dust and 
noise reduction, enhancement of road safety and creation of 
employment opportunities. The policy provides for plantation of 
suitable indigenous species, maintenance of plantations for the 
prescribed period, involvement of agencies i ncluding government 
organizations, Non -Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and self -help 
groups, and use of technology-based monitoring. 
(b)  Plantation and maintenance works are monitored through a 
multi-tier mechanism. Project Directors/Implementation Unit s and 
Regional Offices carry out periodic inspections to verify plantation, 
survival rate and maintenance. 
Independent Engineers/Authority Engineers supervise compliance in 
projects where plantation forms part of civil contracts. Plantation 
progress is rev iewed periodically through review meetings with all 
stakeholders. 
(c)  ‘NHAI Green Highways Excellence Awards’ recognize exemplary 
plantation efforts based on survival rate, vigor, and adherence to 
standard specifications. Conversely, for negligent behavio r, strict 
penal provisions are enforced. 
In case of non -performance, poor maintenance or failure to achieve 
the prescribed survival percentage, contractual provisions provide for 
withholding of payments, recovery of costs, rectification at the 
contractor’s risk and cost, levy of contractual damages/penalties and 
other remedies as per the contract conditions. Payments are linked to 
successful establishment and maintenance of plantations. 
(d)  State/UT-wise details of plantation targets and achievements 
during the last three years are given at Annexure-I.

EXEMPTION OF TOLL 
2065. SHRI N K PREMACHANDRAN: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to exempt State owned public 
transport system from  remittance of toll on National Highway, if so, the 
details of action taken thereon; 
(b) whether the Union Government share the toll collected from NH-66 
with State considering  the share of State for land acquisition cost and 
GST exemption and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Union Government examined the request of KSRTC for 
exempting from paying toll, if so, the details of action taken thereon; 
(d) whether the Government has considered the additional burden of Rs. 
two crores on  KSRTC per month for payment of toll, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(e) whether the Union Government considers the crisis of KSRTC, if so, 
the details thereof; and 
(f) whether the Union Government discourage the State owned public 
transport system, if so, the details of action taken to exempt KSRTC? 
 
  

2 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) Provisions of National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and 
Collection) Rules, 2008 are applicable on all types of transport vehicles 
including State Road Transport Corporations owned or  operated vehicles 
irrespective of its ownership.   
At present, there is no such proposal under co nsideration with 
Government to grant an exemption from the payment of user fees (Toll) 
to State owned public transport undertakings for the use of National 
Highways.   
(b) User fee at fee plazas on National Highways (NHs) is collected 
uniformly across the country in accordance with the provisions of the 
National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 
2008 and the respective Concession Agreements. The revenue collected 
by the Central Government from user fees on NHs, including those in 
Kerala, is deposited into the Consolidated Fund of India (CFI). Funds 
provided through budgetary allocations from the Consolidated Fund of 
India (CFI) are then utilized for the maintenance, development, and 
expansion of National Highways. 
  The contribution of the State Government of Kerala enabled projects 
in Kerala to be given higher priority despite the extremely high cost of 
Land Acquisition (LA) in the State. For development of NH 66 in Kerala, 
total Land Acquisition (LA) cost is about R s. 23,350 crore and 

3 
 
construction cost is about Rs. 28,370 crore. In the total cost, the 
contribution of the State government is Rs. 5,800 crore. 
  Further, there is an overall social and economic benefit to the local 
from the infrastructure development thr ough National Highways. Such 
development contributes to multiple advantages, including the 
expansion of towns and cities and broader economic growth within the 
State.  
(c) to (f) User fee for use of the section of National Highway is levied 
uniformly acros s all States as per the provisions of the NH Fee Rules 
including State Transport Undertaking buses. No blanket exemption from 
the payment of user fees has been provided to State Transport 
Undertakings under the extant Rules.     
There are already various p rovisions under the NH Fee Rules, that 
provide discounts (at Annexure) on user fees for frequent users of 
National Highways across the country. These benefits are also available 
to the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC). 
  
  

4 
 
ANNEXURE

2026 ASKED BY SHRI N K PREMCHANDRAN REGARDING EXEMPTION OF 
TOLL.

Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008: 
  
(i)      For commercial vehicles registered in particular District: Fee for 
commercial vehicle (excluding vehicles plying under National Permit) 
registered in the district where the fee plaza falls shall be 50% of the 
prescribed rate for that category of vehicle, provided no service road or 
alternative road is available for use of such commercial vehicles. 
(ii)    Monthly pass provision for frequent users: Monthly pass provision 
for frequent users by paying 2/3rd fee for 50 single trips for a month. 
(iii)    Return journey pass by paying 1½ times of single fe e for returning 
within 24 hours.

(b) whether the Union Government has any proposal to stop collecting 
toll taxes and to  remove all toll plazas at all NHs across the country in 
view of the above, if so, the details thereof  and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) As per Entry 57 of List II (State List) of the Seventh Schedule to the  
Constitution of India, the subject relating to taxes on vehicles, whether 
mechanically propelled or not, suitable for use on roads, including 
tramcars, subject to the provisions of Entry 35 of List III (Concurrent 
List), falls within the legislative compe tence of the States. Further, 
mechanically propelled vehicles, including the principles on which taxes 
on such vehicles are to be levied, comes under the List III (Concurrent 

2 
 
List). Therefore, taxes on motor vehicles fall within the sole jurisdiction 
of respective State /UT administration, in accordance with constitutional 
provisions. 
Further, the registration fee for motor vehicles is prescribed under Rule 
81 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989. 
(b) User fee at fee plaza is collected for the u se of a completed section 
of National Highway, uniformly across the country in accordance with 
the provisions of the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and 
Collection) Rules, 2008 and the respective Concession Agreements. 
As per the provisions o f National Highways Fee Rules, 2008, in case of 
concessionaire operated fee plaza, the fee notified as per concession 
agreement is collected by the concessionaire till the end of the 
concession period, and after the concession period is over, the fee Plaza  
is handed over to the Government and thereafter the fee is collected by 
the Central Government or the executing authority as per the fee 
specified under the provisions of NH Fee Rules, 2008.  In respect of fee 
plaza under public funded project, the fee le viable shall continue to be 
collected for such section of the National Highway. The revenue 
collected by the Central Government from user fee collection is 
deposited in Consolidated Fund of India (CFI) and the funds provided 
through budgetary allocation fr om the Consolidated Fund of India (CFI) 
are utilised for further maintenance, development and augmentation of 
National Highways.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2068 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
 
PROGRESS UNDER PMKSY 
 
2068. SMT. SANJNA JATAV: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)   the progress made in development of modern food processing infrastructure and       
value-addition facilities under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY); 
(b) the number of projects sanctioned and completed along with the employment 
generated thereunder so far; 
(c) whether any project has been sanctioned under the said scheme in Bharatpur 
Parliamentary Constituency and if so, the details thereof including the present status 
of such project(s) and the number of persons provided employment after completion 
of the said Projects; 
(d) the steps taken to reduce post-harvest losses, promote Farmer Producer Organisations 
(FPOs) and enhance farmers’ income under the scheme; and 
(e) the impact of PMKSY on food processing capacity, exports and overall development 
of the food processing sector? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
 
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing 
the Central Sector umbrella scheme Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) 
across the country. The scheme aims to create modern food processing infrastructure 
and value addition facilities, enhance processing and preservation of agricultural produce, 
generate employment opportunities, and provide better remuneration to farmers. As on 
30.06.2026, a total of 1,735 projects have been approved under various component 
schemes of PMKSY, out of which 1,256 projects have been completed, creating 294.21 
LMT/Annum of processing and preservation capacity and generating 9.16 lakh 
employment opportunities across the country. 
 
(c): Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) is demand driven in nature and 
applications are invited through Expression of Interest (EoI) from all over the country and 
funds are not allocated/sanctioned/released state-wise under any of the component 
schemes of PMKSY. The proposals received are scrutinized for their eligibility and 
evaluated based on the criteria fixed as per the extant scheme guidelines. Merit based 

approvals are given to the eligible proposals based on availability of funds. As on date, 
no project has been sanctioned under PMKSY in Bharatpur Parliamentary Constituency. 
 
(c) & (e): The component schemes under PMKSY provide financial assistance in the form 
of grants-in-aid/subsidy for creation of modern food processing and preservation 
infrastructure with the objective of reducing post-harvest losses and enhancing value 
addition. The creation of food processing infrastructure enhances demand for agricultural 
produce, leading to better price realization and improved income for farmers. PMKSY is a 
demand driven scheme and applications are invited from all eligible applicants, including 
Farmers Producing Organisation (FPOs) through Expression of Interest (EoI). To 
strengthen farmer–producer linkages, PMKSY provides enhanced financial assistance to 
FPOs along with relaxed eligibility conditions such as lower equity contribution, lower 
minimum bank loan requirement and a reduced net-worth requirement compared to the 
general category applicants. Further, Under the centrally sponsored PMFME scheme of the 
Ministry, FPOs are eligible for a 35% credit-linked subsidy up to ₹10 lakh for setting up or 
upgrading micro food processing enterprises, 35% grant of up to ₹3 crore for establishing 
Common Infrastructure and Branding & Marketing support in terms of grant upto 50% for 
groups of FPOs, at State/regional level. 
As on 30.06.2026, 1,256 projects have been completed under PMKSY, benefiting about 
37.76 lakh farmers and creating 294.21 LMT per annum of processing and preservation 
capacity, thereby strengthening the food processing ecosystem, promoting value addition, 
and contributing to the overall exports of food products and growth of the food processing 
sector.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER

DEVELOPMENT OF PUMPED STORAGE PROJECTS IN ASSAM 
 
2069. SHRI AMARSING TISSO: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is promoting Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) to 
facilitate renewable energy integration and meet peak electricity demand 
across the country and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) the number of Pumped Storage Projects under construction and at various 
stages of approval in the country, State-wise;  
 
(c) wheth er any Pumped Storage Project has been identified, proposed or is 
under examination in Assam, particularly in Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao and 
if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(d) whether the Government provides any Central financial assistance or other 
incentives for the development of Pumped Storage Projects and if so, the details 
thereof? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) & (d): The Government has undertaken the following measures to promote 
the development of Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) in the country for 
facilitating renewable energy integration, enhancing grid flexibility, and 
meeting peak electricity demand: 
(i) Ministry of Power h as notified Guidelines to promote development of 
Pumped Storage Projects in the country on 10.04.2023. 
(ii) Budgetary Support towards Cost of Enabling Infrastructure, i.e., 
roads/bridges, railway sidings, ropeways, communication infrastructure and 
transmission line from power house to nearest pooling point.  
(iii) To provide a transparent, fair, standardized procurement framework based 
on open competitive bidding with appropriate risk -sharing between various 
stakeholders, MoP vide Gazette notification dated 06.02.2025 , has notified 
tariff based competitive bidding (TBCB) guidelines for procurement of 
storage capacity/stored energy from pumped storage plants.  
 

 
(iv) The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC), vide its Notification 
dated 26.06.2025, has provided for 100% waiver of Inter-State Transmission 
System (ISTS) charges for Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) for a period of 
25 years from the Commercial Operation Date (COD), in respect of projects 
for which the construction work is awarded on or before 30.06.2028. 
(v) The Government of India, vide Gazette notification dated 01.08.2025, has 
revised the capital expenditure limit for schemes related to setting up hydro 
generating stations to ₹3,000 crore, requiring the concurrence of the Central 
Electricity Authority (CEA ). Further, the Government has exempted off -
stream closed-loop pumped storage schemes, irrespective of the quantum 
of capital expenditure, from the requirement of concurrence by the CEA. 
(vi) Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has revised Guidelines for formul ation 
and concurrence of Detailed Project Report (DPR) of PSPs. Under the revised 
guidelines, the timeline for concurrence of DPR has been reduced from 90 
days to 50 days for PSPs. Further, the clearance of Inter-State Aspects is not 
required for PSPs. 
(vii) Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC), vide its 
notification dated 18.05.2023, has enabled appraisal of PSPs under B2 
category subject to certain conditions.   
(viii) The MoEF&CC on 14.08.2023, has issued specific Terms of Reference (TOR) 
for the proposals involving off stream PSPs wherein collection of baseline 
data for one season (other than monsoon) is prescribed for off stream closed 
loop PSPs and collection of baseline data for two seasons (pre -monsoon & 
post-monsoon) is prescribed for off stream open loop PSPs. 
(ix) The MOEF&CC on 20.08.2024, has extended the provisions relating to survey 
in the forest areas for mining projects to other development projects 
including hydel/PSPs.  
(x) MOEF&CC vide letter dated 10.09.2025  has enhanced the number of 
boreholes for undertaking survey and explorations in the forest area for 
mining and developmental projects including hydel / PSPs. 
(b):  At present, 11 Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) with a total installed 
capacity of 15,870 MW are under construction in the c ountry (Annexure -I). 
Further, 6 PSPs with an aggregate installed capacity of 8,140 MW have been 
concurred/appraised by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) and are yet to be 
taken up for construction (Annexure -II). In addition, 1 PSP with an installed 
capacity of 640 MW is presently under examination in the CEA (Annexure-III).  
(c):   As per the records of the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), 6 Pumped 
Storage Projects (PSPs) with an aggregate installed capacity of 6,220 MW have 
been identified in the  State of Assam. Of these, 4 PSPs are at the Survey & 
Investigation (S&I) stage. The details are provided at Annexure-IV.
